item.title: China's old-age dependency ratio overtakes children for first time
item.description: China is now supporting more people aged 65 and above than children, underscoring the impact of its rapidly ageing population and a declining birth rate.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China is now supporting more people aged 65 and above than children, underscoring the impact of its rapidly ageing population and a declining birth rate. Data from China's National Bureau of Statistics showed the old-age dependency ratio — the non-working-age population compared to the working-age population — was 23.1% in 2025, compared with 22% for children, Chinese state-affiliated media Yicai reported The ratio has risen steadily over the years, up from 15% in 2016 to more than 20% in 2021 There are now more than 223 million people in China aged 65 and above compared with around 213 million children aged 14 and under, the data showed China's population fell for a fourth straight year in 2025, as its birth rate dropped to a record low The country's birth rate has been falling for decades, a result of the one-child policy in place from 1980 to 2015, as well as rapid urbanisation Authorities have rolled out a range of measures to encourage marriage and childbearing, including family subsidies, childcare support, and reduced childbirth-related medical costs They have also pledged to make urban life more supportive for young people, children and families

item.title: Natural gas is losing its grip across key power markets
item.description: Natural gas was supposed to be the dominant bridge fuel between legacy generation systems and a clean-powered future. But across key markets in Europe and Asia, power producers appear to be increasingly bypassing the fuel in favour of other options.
item.dc:creator: Gavin Maguire
item.content:encoded: Natural gas was supposed to be the dominant bridge fuel between legacy generation systems and a clean-powered future. But across key markets in Europe and Asia, power producers appear to be increasingly bypassing the fuel in favour of other options. Total electricity generation from gas-fired power plants has contracted this year from 2025 in the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Turkey, Japan, South Korea and China, according to data from think tank Ember. Those countries represent some of the key traditional and high-potential gas markets for gas power generation, and yet all simultaneously pared back gas use this year as global supplies and prices were impacted by the war in the Middle East. Significantly, total electricity generation across those six nations has expanded this year despite lower collective gas-fired output, resulting in natural gas losing share to other generation sources within those key power networks. For exporters of liquefied natural gas, the risk is that gas remains essential as a marginal fuel but ceases to be a growth engine for power generation. Power systems still need gas-fired plants to bolster reliability, but they appear to need progressively less gas-fired electricity from those facilities as renewable generation, storage and output from other power sources expand. That is a challenging outlook for an industry investing heavily in new export capacity on the assumption that tomorrow's power sector will burn substantially more gas than today's. SHARE SQUEEZE The steady erosion of natural gas' share within a wide span of key power sectors underscores the problem for gas market bulls. In the Netherlands, home to Europe's main gas trading hub, the gas share of electricity generation during the first nine months of 2026 was just under 32%. That's the lowest reading on record for that period and compares to a nearly 60% gas share in the same months in 2020 and nearly 40% in 2022. In the United Kingdom, the closure of the country's last remaining coal power plant in late 2024 was expected to trigger a sustained upturn in gas use. Yet gas' share of the utility mix plumbed a new low of 29% so far this year, compared to roughly 41% in the same months in 2022. And in Turkey, which was long considered a viable growth market for gas due to its fast-growing manufacturing base, gas' share of the generation mix this year has dropped to just under 11%. That compares to an average 32% gas share in 2021, which is when Turkey's gas-fired generation total hit a record and spurred optimism among gas exporters that the country would continue to steadily increase its gas needs. Gas has also lost ground across key Asian markets. In Japan, which for years has been one of the top LNG importers, gas use in electricity generation has lost ground to both rising output from renewables and a recovery in output from the country's nuclear reactor fleet. The gas share of Japan's electricity mix so far this year was 28.4%, which was the first reading on record below 30%, and compares to an average share of around 35% in 2022 and nearly 40% in 2019. South Korea's power system also reduced gas' share to a multi-year low of just under 29% this year, while in China gas' share of the mix was just 3.07%, which again was a record low. ABSOLUTE PEAK? For gas market bulls, the trends in absolute levels of gas-fired generation are also likely to be a cause for concern. In all six of the key markets noted above, year-to-date generation from gas-fired power plants has posted a decline this year, just as output from many other sources has increased in 2026. In Europe, higher output from renewables installations alongside battery storage networks has allowed most utilities to boost total electricity supplies while cutting overall gas generation. In Turkey, a jump in hydro power production to the highest in over five years also allowed for lower gas consumption. In Asia, power producers dialled up generation from cheaper coal-fired power stations to accommodate tighter gas supplies, which have been hampered by the US and Israeli war against Iran and the subsequent drops in [USN:S8N40Y05J TEXT:"LNG shipments from Qatar"]. The worrying signal for LNG producers is that this decline has occurred even before a new wave of gas export capacity comes online. Major suppliers are investing billions of dollars on the assumption that power demand growth will translate into rising gas consumption for decades to come. Yet across several of the world's most important gas-burning economies, utilities are finding ways to grow electricity supplies while reducing reliance on gas-fired generation. If that pattern spreads further, the industry's challenge may not be securing enough supply to meet future demand, but finding enough demand to absorb future supply. Gas may remain indispensable in many modern power systems, but the latest generation trends suggest it is increasingly valued for reliability rather than volume. That's an uncomfortable distinction for exporters betting on sustained growth. The opinions expressed here are those of the author , a columnist for Reuters. Enjoying this column? item.title: UBS meets expectations with $2.7 billion Q3 profit
item.description: UBS reported a third-quarter net profit of $2.69 billion on Wednesday, up 8% year-on-year and roughly in line with the $2.71 billion expected as per a company-provided consensus forecast.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: UBS (UBSG.S) reported a third-quarter net profit of $2.69 billion on Wednesday, up 8% year-on-year and roughly in line with the $2.71 billion expected as per a company-provided consensus forecast. The performance of the largest Swiss bank was supported by net new assets of $55 billion in global wealth management, driven by inflows of $18 billion in Asia and $17 billion in the Americas. Profitability in the Americas improved, with the profit-before-tax margin up by over 2 percentage points, UBS said. The integration of former rival Credit Suisse is on track for completion by year-end, the bank added, with cumulative cost savings by end-2026 now expected at around $13.7 billion, up from around $13.5 billion. Staff levels dropped by almost 1,500 full-time employees in the quarter as integration progressed. Employees at the bank are running more than 12,700 personal AI agents and the bank keeps investing in the technology, UBS said. The bank's cost-income ratio dropped to 72.3% at the end of the third quarter from 77% a year earlier. UBS repurchased $1.8 billion of shares in the quarter and plans to complete its buyback program of $3 billion in February, rather than by the mid-2027 timeline it had announced previously. The bank has [USN:L1N43V04F TEXT:"conditioned"] the amount and pace of share buybacks on the outcome of a Swiss banking rules overhaul that follows the 2023 collapse of Credit Suisse and its state-engineered emergency takeover by UBS. New capital rules for UBS are currently being [USN:L1N45N0NB TEXT:"debated"] in a parliamentary committee and expected to reach the lower house floor in December. The Swiss upper house last month [USN:L8N45F0DE TEXT:"proposed"] rules that UBS suggested were unacceptable. UBS's chairman has warned the bank would need to carefully [USN:L8N4590WE TEXT:"consider"] its future in Switzerland if capital requirements are too harsh, and some shareholders have called for UBS to [USN:L1N45N061 TEXT:"leave"] Switzerland. UBS hopes that parliament will reach a solution that supports Switzerland's financial stability without imposing undue costs on UBS's shareholders, clients and employees, the bank said in its results presentation.

item.title: Equinor profit doubles as Middle East war lifts oil, gas prices
item.description: Equinor on Wednesday reported its strongest quarterly profit in almost four years, driven by a surge in oil and gas prices as the war in the Middle East continued to disrupt global energy supplies, and raised its full-year output target.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Equinor (EQNR.OL) on Wednesday reported its strongest quarterly profit in almost four years, driven by a surge in oil and gas prices as the war in the Middle East continued to disrupt global energy supplies, and raised its full-year output target. The Norwegian group's adjusted earnings before tax for the July to September period rose to $12.34 billion from $6.22 billion a year earlier, slightly ahead of the $12.19 billion predicted in a poll of 21 analysts compiled by Equinor. "High production in the third quarter enabled us to capture additional value from higher prices," CEO Anders Opedal said in a statement. Equinor now expects its oil and gas output to rise by around 4% this year, up from 3% growth seen previously. The shares of majority state-owned Equinor are up 86% year-to-date, trading at all-time highs in recent weeks. They are outperforming a 43% increase in European energy stocks (.SXEP) , reflecting Equinor's position as a major supplier of oil and gas to Europe and with no direct exposure to the Middle East.

item.title: BNP Paribas beats Q3 profit forecast, unveils €1.3 billion share buyback
item.description: BNP Paribas posted a forecast-beating rise in third-quarter profit on Wednesday, aided by its investment bankers, as the lender announced a €1.3 billion ($1.45 billion) share buyback and played down the impact of soaring government bond yields.
item.dc:creator: Mateusz Rabiega
item.content:encoded: BNP Paribas (BNPP.PA) posted a forecast-beating rise in third-quarter profit on Wednesday, aided by its investment bankers, as the lender announced a €1.3 billion ($1.45 billion) share buyback and played down the impact of soaring government bond yields. France's BNP said quarterly net income climbed 14% to €3.46 billion, beating the €3.23 billion average forecast of analysts polled by the bank. Revenue at the euro zone's biggest bank by assets rose year-on-year to €13.76 billion, slightly above expectations. BNP is reporting alongside a flurry of European banks this week including Deutsche Bank (DBKGn.DE) , UBS (UBSG.S) , and Santander (SAN.MC) , with investors watching closely to see if lenders can sustain recent record profits. HSBC on Tuesday sent a chill through the sector after it [USN:L2N46D02S TEXT:"disappointed "]with its revenue growth, sending its shares down nearly 7%. French banks face further challenges, with soaring euro zone sovereign bond yields - [USN:L6N4680JY TEXT:"especially in France"] amid concerns about the country's fiscal position - [USN:L6N4610RI TEXT:"reviving worries about lenders' exposure to government debt."] BNP said its exposure to French sovereign bonds was limited, roughly at €19 billion at end-September and that France accounted for under 10% of its pre-tax income last year. EQUITY TRADING JUMPS The French lender's results were helped for a second consecutive quarter by a record jump in equity and prime services revenue. The 50% rise year-on-year surpassed the average 37% gain in equities trading across the top five US players, according to a Reuters calculation from company statements. Overall sales at BNP's corporate and institutional banking unit, which long-time CEO Jean-Laurent Bonnafe has made critical to its success, rose by 17% year-on-year. Fixed-income, currencies and commodities trading revenue was flat, reflecting an [USN:L4N4600TB TEXT:"industry wide"] weak quarter for fixed income. BNP's retail business saw income rise by 4%, boosted by higher interest rates. The bank said it would launch a €1.3 billion share buyback in November after it met its Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio, a key measure of financial strength, at end-June, ahead of schedule. RBC analysts said before the results they expected BNP to bring forward a buyback totalling €1.2 billion euros "to express confidence in its outlook". ($1 = 0.8961 euros)

item.title: Colten Ellis stops 23 shots as Sabres shut out Sharks
item.description: Colten Ellis made 23 saves for the Buffalo Sabres to earn his second career shutout in a 2-0 win against the host San Jose Sharks on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Colten Ellis made 23 saves for the Buffalo Sabres to earn his second career shutout in a 2-0 win against the host San Jose Sharks on Tuesday. It was Ellis' first appearance since getting pulled early in the second period on Oct. 12 against the Florida Panthers, when he gave up two goals on nine shots. His lone previous shutout came on April 9 against the Columbus Blue Jackets Olen Zellweger and Zach Benson scored for the Sabres, who snapped a three-game skid (0-1-2). Owen Power assisted on both tallies. Yaroslav Askarov made 38 saves for the Sharks, who have lost two in a row. Zellweger put Buffalo up 1-0 early in the second period. Konsta Helenius took a feed from Power inside his own zone to the red line and dished it over to Zellweger. The smooth-skating defenseman carried it up the left wing before snapping it from the top of the circle inside the far post 50 seconds into the frame. Benson scored an empty-net goal at 19:05 of the third period. He stole the puck from Ivar Stenberg in the San Jose zone and held off the rookie in a battle toward the net, swatting the puck in for his first of the season. The two sides traded chances in the first period, with Buffalo edging San Jose 16-12 in shots on goal through 20 minutes. Midway through the period, Askarov denied Jack Quinn with a chest save on a chance off the rush. Late in the frame, Ellis got his blocker on a quick shot from Adam Gaudette from the slot on a power play. A minute and a half later, Askarov stopped Tage Thompson from the high slot and then sprawled to swallow up the rebound with Benson on the doorstep. The Sabres outshot the Sharks 14-4 in the second period, but Ellis was sharp despite limited activity, including a stop on Collin Graf off a feed from Macklin Celebrini. Late in the third, Ellis denied Kiefer Sherwood, closing the pads in time to hold off the forward's shot from the slot. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brewers sell out World Series watch party as fans await first title
item.description: MILWAUKEE -- More than 30,000 title-starved Brewers fans turned out to watch a baseball game played 1,200 miles away, but they will have to wait at least one more day to see their dream fulfilled.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE -- More than 30,000 title-starved Brewers fans turned out to watch a baseball game played 1,200 miles away, but they will have to wait at least one more day to see their dream fulfilled. The visiting Milwaukee Brewers were on the brink of the first World Series title in franchise history when the Tampa Bay Rays rallied for two runs in the bottom of the 12th inning to avoid a sweep in Game 4 and stay alive with a 4-3 victory Tuesday night in St. Petersburg, Fla. After winning the first two games at home, the Brewers hosted watch parties at American Family Field for Games 3 and 4, with ticket sales capped at 31,000 for each game. Proceeds from the $15 tickets benefited the Brewers Community Foundation, the team's official charitable arm. The Brewers have not yet announced an official watch party for Game 5 on Wednesday night, although one is expected. Even with hordes of Brewers fans making the trip to Tropicana Field, each of the first two official watch parties in Milwaukee sold out within 20 minutes, according to MLB.com. Fans filled all three decks of the 41,900-seat stadium from foul pole to foul pole, with only the outfield sections unsold. Dozens of bars, restaurants and gathering places throughout the Milwaukee metropolitan area and across Wisconsin also hosted watch parties. The Brewers, whose only other World Series appearance was a seven-game loss to the St. Louis Cardinals in 1982, issued nearly 100 media credentials for the Tuesday watch party, said Megan Kendall of the Brewers' media relations. Tickets for the Game 4 watch party at the stadium were selling for $293 on the secondary market one hour before game time. Facebook Marketplace was filled with "ISO" (in search of) postings from fans still looking for last-minute tickets to watch the game on the 12,077-square-foot screen in center field. But it wasn't just the fans who were caught up in the postseason enthusiasm. "I'm just so excited to be here," said Debra Dinsmore, a member of Brewers' guest relations who greets fans with a smile at almost every home game from her post at one of the escalators near the right field gate. "At the beginning, I wasn't sure, but at this point I'm glad we're here and we're doing it tonight." Kay Kenealy of nearby Waukesha, Wis., had a 20-game ticket package during the regular season and attended the first two World Series games in Milwaukee. "It just sounded like a crazy, fun thing to do. So I decided to do it," said Kenealy, who said she has been a Brewers fan since the team moved to Milwaukee in 1970 as the relocated Seattle Pilots. "You get the stadium atmosphere without having to fly 1,200 miles to do it." "If not tonight, then tomorrow night," Kenealy said. "I do not need them to come back to Milwaukee to win the World Series. I want them to get it done." --Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

item.title: India's GST clarification on brokerage modestly positive for FPIs, analysts say
item.description: The Indian government's clarification that brokerage paid by overseas clients can qualify as exports and avoid goods and services tax (GST), subject to certain conditions, is sentimentally positive for foreign investors, analysts said, at a time when record outflows have battered domestic stocks.
item.dc:creator: Vivek M
item.content:encoded: The Indian government's clarification that brokerage paid by overseas clients can qualify as exports and avoid goods and services tax (GST), subject to certain conditions, is sentimentally positive for foreign investors, analysts said, at a time when record outflows have battered domestic stocks. The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs in a circular dated October 26 said that brokerage paid through repatriable rupee accounts, from which funds can be moved out of India, could count as an export of services and therefore be exempt from GST. India levies 18% GST on brokerage fees. Full-service brokers typically charge brokerage between 0.01% and 0.55% on the value of shares traded. The clarification could reduce the GST burden on foreign portfolio investors, and any increase in trading volumes would be positive for brokerage firms and depositories, Jefferies said in a note on Tuesday. Foreign investors have offloaded Indian shares worth $32.66 billion so far this year, well above the previous annual record of $18.91 billion in 2025, according to National Securities Depository data. India's benchmark Nifty 50 index (.NSEI) is down 13.6% in 2026, setting the stage for its worst annual performance in over a decade, while MSCI's emerging markets index (.dMIEF00000PUS) has risen 12.4%. The GST clarification is "sentimentally positive but may not make much of a difference, especially for FPI mood.... However, a decision on capital gains (tax) could provide much needed relief," said Ambareesh Baliga, an independent market analyst in Mumbai. The move comes amid speculation about a potential cut in the capital gains tax. The Indian Express newspaper earlier this week reported that the government is discussing lowering long-term capital gains tax from 12.5% for both domestic and foreign investors in the run-up to the federal budget next year.

item.title: GAIL India to invest $63 million in heating unit at Ratnagiri LNG terminal, executive says
item.description: GAIL India is investing 6 billion rupees ($63.1 million) to build a heating unit at its Ratnagiri LNG terminal to help it gasify the super-chilled fuel, the company's business development director told reporters on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: GAIL India (GAIL.NS) is investing 6 billion rupees ($63.1 million) to build a heating unit at its Ratnagiri LNG terminal to help it gasify the super-chilled fuel, the company's business development director told reporters on Wednesday. The facility, due to be completed by June 2027, will enable the company to run the LNG terminal at its full capacity of 5 million tons per annum, R. K. Singhal said at an industry event. The facility is operating at about 50% capacity as the heating unit is not ready, Singhal said. The Ratnagiri facility was generating heat through the waste of a power plant operated by another entity to gasify the fuel. That plant is not functional now, he said. GAIL is also building a small size captive power plant to generate heat for the liquefied natural gas facility, he added. ($1 = 95.1150 Indian rupees)

item.title: Philippines will defend peso 'as hard as we possibly can', president says
item.description: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr said on Wednesday authorities would do all they can to ensure the peso does not keep falling against the dollar.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr said on Wednesday authorities would do all they can to ensure the peso does not keep falling against the dollar. "People can take solace in the fact that our policy towards the peso is to continue to defend the peso as hard as we possibly can," Marcos told reporters. Marcos said the government has "all the means to defend" the currency, which hit a record low of 64.17 to the dollar on Tuesday There was no reason to panic over its weakness, he said "Our foreign exchange reserves are healthy. And that’s what we draw on to defend the peso," he added Philippine foreign reserves fell to $99.5 billion in September, the lowest level since September 2023 The peso has lost more than 8% against the dollar so far this year The governor of the central bank last week said it intervenes in the foreign exchange market to smooth out sharp fluctuations The central bank raised its key policy rate by a [USN:L1N46809C TEXT:"larger-than-expected 50 basis points"] last week to combat inflation, which it said could be fueled by a weaker peso through higher imports Marcos, who had met central bank officials on Tuesday, said monetary measures could only do so much to control inflation, adding "we have to do others"

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan's Nidec (6594.T) will likely not be able to obtain an auditor's opinion on its securities report by month-end after an auditor said an audit would not be completed in time, the Nikkei business daily reported on Wednesday. The Japanese electric motor maker will submit internal control documents to the Tokyo Stock Exchange by the deadline without the opinion from the auditor PwC Japan, seeking early review on listing maintenance, the Nikkei reported without citing sources. Nidec said [USN:L2N46D09T TEXT:"on Tuesday"] it had decided to sue founder Shigenobu Nagamori and eight other former executives for damages over suspected accounting irregularities that have put its stock market listing at risk.

item.title: Weak domestic returns fuel India's overseas retail investing boom
item.description: India's top money managers are launching a flurry of funds in a tax-neutral hub to absorb the record sums that domestic investors are sending overseas, frustrated by weak returns at home and craving exposure to AI-related assets.
item.dc:creator: Jayshree Pyasi, Dharamraj Dhutia
item.content:encoded: India's top money managers are launching a flurry of funds in a tax-neutral hub to absorb the record sums that domestic investors are sending overseas, frustrated by weak returns at home and craving exposure to AI-related assets. At least half a dozen such funds have been launched in the past six months, including the JioBlackRock Advantage World Equity Fund this week by the joint venture of Mukesh Ambani's Jio Financial (JIOF.NS) and BlackRock (BLK.N) , the world's largest asset manager. The overseas investment rush poses a dilemma for policymakers, who have spent years encouraging households to move savings from real estate, gold and bank deposits into domestic equities. The world's most populous nation has more than 130 million retail stock investors, many of whom are scouring for investment targets abroad, from New York to Kazakhstan, after sustained underperformance in the domestic stock market. "Over the last two years, we've seen a clear increase in demand for global assets," said Shobhit Mathur, co-founder of money manager Ionic Asset. "Investors are no longer looking at overseas exposure as a tactical allocation but increasingly as a permanent part of portfolio construction." International investments by individuals in India either directly or through funds more than doubled from a year earlier to nearly $2.3 billion in the first half of 2026, on track to surpass the 2025 full year's record $2.65 billion, data from the central bank, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), showed. One such investor is Ankit Khandelwal, a 41-year-old resident of Kota in the western Indian state of Rajasthan who invests in global exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and companies listed in markets such as Kazakhstan and Mongolia. "It began as an experiment but since then better returns overseas and persistent rupee weakness has led me to grow the overseas portion of my portfolio to over 60% from about 5% in early 2025," said Khandelwal, who is an import and export adviser to companies, adding that he understands metals, mining and energy firms of the world. India's rupee currency hit a record low this year as its stock market suffered sustained selling by institutional investors and as its economy was hit by rising energy costs from the Iran war. The South Asian nation caps overseas remittances at an annual $250,000 per person because its currency is not fully convertible. The benchmark Nifty 50 index (.NSEI) is down 5.3% over the last two years, compared with a 47% gain in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index (.dMIEF00000PUS) and a 32% rise in the S&P 500 (.SPX) in the US. High valuations and a lack of AI-related stocks have also weighed on returns from local equities. Little wonder then that retail trading account openings for domestic investments fell by a quarter to 33 million in the fiscal year ending March 2026, data from Indian depositories showed. GIFT CITY The RBI restricts Indian funds to a maximum cumulative overseas investment of $7 billion and a $1 billion limit for an individual asset manager. With the limits almost exhausted, funds cannot create fresh units to invest at will even as demand grows. But these limits do not apply to overseas investment funds of domestic asset managers launched through the GIFT City tax-neutral hub located in India's western Gujarat state. Thus, besides JioBlackRock, HDFC Asset Management, Parag Parikh and Aditya Birla Sun Life have launched such funds in the last six months. Other domestic funds that invest in foreign equities too are sought after, despite the RBI limits. Assets in overseas fund-of-funds schemes rose 42% year-on-year to 488 billion rupees in September, while investors registered for such investments climbed 34% to nearly 2 million, according to data published by the Association of Mutual Funds in India. The paucity of overseas investment avenues for Indian investors has driven some overseas ETFs to trade at hefty premiums to their net asset values. One such fund, the Motilal Oswal Nasdaq Q50 ETF, traded as much as 65% to 80% above the value of its underlying portfolio at times in September, while some Mirae Asset overseas ETFs commanded premiums of 27% to 58%. REGULATORS CAUTIOUS Retail investors are also racing to gain direct exposure to US and other overseas stocks, with discount brokers Groww (BILO.NS) , Zerodha and Angel One (ANGO.NS) launching fractional investing platforms this month. Similar investment trends are underway in a number of markets, [USN:L4N4560L0 TEXT:"including China"], where regulators have tightened scrutiny of unofficial channels through which money is being sent overseas. Indian authorities are cautious about the money flowing abroad from such investments but are not considering measures to curb such flows, three people at Indian regulators told Reuters. Emails to India's market regulator and the RBI, which sets overseas investment limits, were not answered. Some industry executives voiced caution. "Indian markets have not given returns and overseas markets are looking attractive," said Swarup Mohanty, chief executive of Mirae Asset Investment Managers. "If you want to invest for diversification then it's fine, but investing purely to chase short-term returns is worrying." ($1 = 95.1350 Indian rupees)

item.title: Canucks halt 10-game skid with late 3-goal rally, OT win vs. Ducks
item.description: Jonathan Lekkerimaki scored twice in the final three minutes of regulation and Filip Hronek scored on a two-man advantage in overtime as the visiting Vancouver Canucks snapped a 10-game losing streak with a 6-5 victory over the Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jonathan Lekkerimaki scored twice in the final three minutes of regulation and Filip Hronek scored on a two-man advantage in overtime as the visiting Vancouver Canucks snapped a 10-game losing streak with a 6-5 victory over the Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday. Liam Ohgren, Brock Boeser and Jamie Oleksiak also scored for the Canucks, who trailed 5-2 with less than eight minutes remaining in regulation and won for the first time since Oct. 3. Boeser and Elias Pettersson each had two assists. Leevi Merilainen made 18 saves for Vancouver, which scored the winner with 10.4 seconds remaining in overtime on a one-timer by Hronek from the slot. A.J. Greer scored twice and Jackson LaCombe had three assists as the Ducks lost for the sixth time in their past seven games. Leo Carlsson and Jeff Malott each had a goal and an assist while Beckett Sennecke also scored for Anaheim. Lukas Dostal made 27 saves for the Ducks, who lost for the eighth time in nine home games against the Canucks since December 2021. With Vancouver trailing 5-3, Lekkerimaki beat Dostal from inside the left circle at 17:14 of the third period, then tied the game on a shot through traffic from beyond the left circle with just under two minutes remaining in regulation. The Ducks took a 1-0 lead just over four minutes into the game when Greer scored off Hronek's stick. Vancouver drew even 6:36 into the second period when Ohgren put a rebound past Dostal after a shot hit Anaheim's Tristan Luneau. The Ducks went ahead 2-1 just 30 seconds later when Malott tapped in a centering pass from LaCombe. Sennecke made it 3-1 at 15:44 of the second period on the power play when the puck caromed off his left leg following a shot by Cutter Gauthier. Carlsson scored at 18:24 to extend the lead to 4-1. The Canucks pulled within 4-2 on Boeser's goal at 11:40 of the third, but the Ducks answered 43 seconds later when Greer deflected the puck in from the edge of the crease for a 5-2 advantage. Oleksiak set the stage for Lekkerimaki's late heroics with an unassisted goal at 12:54 to cut Vancouver's deficit to 5-3. --Field Level Media

item.title: AI chips worth $12.1 million seized at Malaysia airport, customs authority says
item.description: Malaysian customs said on Wednesday that it had seized about 49.5 million ringgit ($12.11 million) worth of advanced artificial intelligence chips this month, as authorities close in on a syndicate suspected of smuggling high-performance semiconductors through the country's main airport.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Malaysian customs said on Wednesday that it had seized about 49.5 million ringgit ($12.11 million) worth of advanced artificial intelligence chips this month, as authorities close in on a syndicate suspected of smuggling high-performance semiconductors through the country's main airport. Malaysia [USN:L6N3TB03O TEXT:"imposed export controls"] last year on the movement of advanced AI chips of US origin, following pressure from the United States to stem their flow into China On October 15, authorities found 30 server units containing advanced AI chips during an inspection at Kuala Lumpur International Airport's free trade zone, the airport's customs director Aspalila Ag Tuah told reporters Initial investigations found that the shipment, originating from an Asian country, was to be re-exported to another nation in the continent, a move that required a trade permit, she said "The servers were falsely declared as electronic components... and shipped through Malaysia to ensure there would be no restrictions imposed while being exported to the next destination," Aspalila said A Malaysian firm that facilitated the shipment has been called in to assist investigations, he added The shipment was suspected to have been carried out by a network responsible for a [USN:L6N42X0OH TEXT:"similar smuggling attempt"] foiled by customs authorities in June, she said At least five cases were linked to the syndicate, involving seizures of chips worth more than 100 million ringgit in total, she said, declining to divulge further details citing an ongoing probe ($1 = 4.0870 ringgit)

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vietnam's [USN:L4N3SU0A4 TEXT:"International Financial Center"] said on Wednesday its first 10 members are expected to mobilise and invest about $2.7 billion in the country's business hub Ho Chi Minh City through 2027. Among the initial 10 members are holding companies linked to Keppel Asset Management, AG&P LNG and VinaCapital International Partners, the centre said in a statement. Those members are expected to invest about $2.7 billion and have disclosed commitments to mobilise more than $2 billion for infrastructure, energy, data centres, education and renewable energy projects, it said In addition, Keppel is exploring co-investment platforms with global partners that could mobilise up to $1 billion more, it said The government is focusing on international financial centres in Ho Chi Minh City and Danang as part of a broader strategy to attract foreign investment, deepen capital markets and strengthen Vietnam's role in regional finance Under legislation approved last year, financial centre members will be allowed to access international financing and conduct transactions in foreign currencies The centres will operate under international accounting and financial standards, including capital adequacy and liquidity requirements applicable to both domestic and foreign-owned banks

item.title: Raphael Lavoie's first NHL goal leads Golden Knights past Senators
item.description: Raphael Lavoie's first NHL goal was the go-ahead tally midway through the third period as the Vegas Golden Knights earned a 4-1 victory over the Ottawa Senators on Tuesday night in Las Vegas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Raphael Lavoie's first NHL goal was the go-ahead tally midway through the third period as the Vegas Golden Knights earned a 4-1 victory over the Ottawa Senators on Tuesday night in Las Vegas. Braeden Bowman, William Karlsson and Jack Eichel also scored goals for Vegas, which snapped a season-high three-game losing streak (0-2-1). Adin Hill stopped 25 shots for the win. Shane Pinto scored a goal and Jonas Johansson stopped 25 of 27 shots for Ottawa, which was playing the first game of a five-game road trip. The Senators have alternated wins and losses for eight games. Ottawa, which outshot Vegas 11-4 in the opening period, nearly took a 1-0 lead at the start of the second period. However, Hill made a highlight-reel save on Tim Stutzle's backdoor one-timer from the right side of the net, diving across the crease and sticking his arm out to block the shot. Vegas jumped in front with 11 seconds remaining in the second period on a power-play goal by Bowman. He tapped in a rebound of an Ivan Barbashev shot in front of the crease. The score came just after Hill had raced out to the right circle to poke the puck away from Ridly Greig as he broke in on a breakaway. Ottawa tied it 33 seconds into the third period on a power-play goal by Pinto. He went in on a breakaway and fired a wrist shot past Hill's low glove side and inside the right post. The Golden Knights regained the lead 2-1 at the 8:01 mark when Lavoie slammed in the rebound of a Nic Dowd shot inside the right post. Lavoie, 26, was playing in his 27th career NHL game, his 10th this season. Vegas sealed the win with a pair of empty-net goals, the first by Karlsson on a breakaway with two minutes left, the second on Eichel's backhand shot from the blue line with seven seconds to go. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rio Tinto proposes 56% pay jump for CEO as mining sector fights for talent
item.description: Rio Tinto's , board has proposed increasing its CEO Simon Trott's target remuneration package by 56% to £9.8 million ($13.06 million), according to four people familiar with the matter and documents reviewed by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Melanie Burton, Clara Denina
item.content:encoded: Rio Tinto's (RIO.AX) , (RIO.L) board has proposed increasing its CEO Simon Trott's target remuneration package by 56% to £9.8 million ($13.06 million), according to four people familiar with the matter and documents reviewed by Reuters. Surging pay at defence, aerospace and energy transition firms has left mining companies including Rio Tinto — the world's second-biggest listed miner — scrambling to compete for top talent. Rio Tinto's board has expanded its peer benchmarking group — the list of companies it compares itself to when calculating executive compensation ranges — an investor presentation seen by Reuters showed. Among other companies, it added US energy majors Chevron (CVX.N) and ExxonMobil (XOM.N) as well as GE Aerospace (GE.N) . Responding to Reuters questions about the changes, Ben Wyatt, who chairs Rio Tinto's remuneration committee, said the miner was consulting investors ahead of a policy update. He said Trott's fixed pay would remain unchanged but incentives tied to multiyear business outcomes and shareholder returns would be adjusted. "This is designed to drive business performance in the interests of shareholders, support the delivery of Rio Tinto's long-term strategy, and attract and retain strong leadership in a competitive global market," he said in a statement. Appointed in July 2025, Trott delivered a [USN:L4N43U2OW TEXT:"43% jump in first-half underlying earnings"] this year while pursuing restructuring and asset sales. SOME INVESTORS CONCERNED ABOUT CEO PAY INFLATION, BAD OPTICS Reflecting a compensation overhaul weighted to performance, Trott's maximum remuneration is proposed to grow 63% to £18.3 million, the briefing documents showed. Short-term incentives would rise to a maximum of 300% of base salary from 200%, while long-term targets would jump to 900% from 500%. Trott's new package would apply to the next three years of his compensation. To come into effect, the expanded framework will require shareholder approval at next year's annual meeting. Some Rio Tinto investors, however, told Reuters they were concerned the compensation proposal could fuel salary inflation among top Australian mining executives and, amid a cost-of-living crisis, reflect poorly on the company. GLOBAL RUSH TO SECURE TOP LEADERS DRIVES UP CEO PAY A Deloitte report in April showed that median CEO pay at FTSE 100 companies increased 18% year-on-year to £5.89 million in 2025. Executive pay in Britain's aerospace, engineering and manufacturing sectors in particular has surged in the past two years. And as competition for top leaders heats up — both across sectors and within a mining industry pivoting toward energy transition metals — mining executives are already moving or being approached. Rag Udd is leaving BHP (BHP.AX) to become CEO of Albemarle (ALB.N) , while French miner Eramet (ERMT.PA) approached Rio Tinto's Jerome Pecresse for its CEO position within the past year, according to one person close to the matter. Both Albemarle and Eramet are developing lithium projects for electric vehicle batteries. Pecresse, who Rio Tinto recruited from General Electric, did not respond to a request for comment. Eramet and Rio Tinto declined to comment. BRIDGING THE TRANSATLANTIC PAY GAP Companies outside the United States are also increasing pay to bridge a widening transatlantic divide. Nearly 60% of FTSE 350 companies proposed pay increases during this year's annual general meeting cycle, data from proxy advisory services firm Glass Lewis showed. Under Rio Tinto's proposed changes, Trott's maximum package would place him just under the median of the 19 companies the miner considers peers. US oil major ExxonMobil's CEO Darren Woods, who earned $33 million in 2025, topped that list, the documents showed. Canada's Agnico Eagle Mines (AEM.TO) and US miner Freeport-McMoRan (FCX.N) were the highest-ranked mining companies in the peer group. If approved, Trott's pay increase would put him among the top tier of Australian CEOs and ahead of rival miner BHP's Brandon Craig, whose remuneration is expected to be around $10 million and is capped at just below $13 million. Such pay gaps could put pressure on other companies to follow Rio Tinto's lead, investors and analysts say. Total median pay for CEOs and CFOs already jumped 14% this year through performance-linked incentives, according to a Bedford Group report on mining industry compensation. Yet some shareholder resistance remains. Last year, Anglo American (AAL.L) [USN:L4N3XE0FE TEXT:"withdrew a proposal"] to guarantee substantial bonuses for senior executives tied to its Teck Resources (TECKb.TO) merger. But others, including George Cheveley, portfolio manager at Rio Tinto shareholder Ninety One, said higher pay can be a useful tool to boost performance. "As long as it is aligned with shareholders, I'm quite happy," Cheveley said in response to a generic question about mining executive pay. ($1 = 0.7505 pounds)

item.title: Businesses and investors of Ambani's Jio as it debuts on Indian bourses
item.description: Jio Platforms shares soared 21% in their Mumbai debut on Wednesday, giving India's biggest-ever initial public offering a roaring start and Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries its first listing in two decades.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jio Platforms (JIOP.NS) shares soared 21% in their Mumbai debut on Wednesday, giving India's biggest-ever initial public offering a roaring start and Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries its first listing in two decades. The listing of the company, whose main business is telecoms, marks the first public listing from Reliance (RELI.NS) since 2006. Here are facts and numbers on Jio Platforms, which counts Meta (META.O) and Google among its major foreign investors: TELECOMS BUSINESS Reliance Jio Platforms is a unit of Ambani's oil-to-retail conglomerate Reliance Industries (RELI.NS) . It is best known for the telecom business Reliance Jio Infocomm, which is the country's biggest player with more than 500 million subscribers. Launched in 2016, the telecom business, popularly referred to simply as Jio, hit rivals such as Bharti Airtel (BRTI.NS) and Vodafone Idea (VODA.NS) hard by offering free voice and data plans initially. The move, in line with Ambani's [USN:L4N35S18O TEXT:"typical strategy"] of offering ultra-low prices to lure consumers, drove up its customer base and allowed many Indians to access platforms such as YouTube and Facebook for the first time. Jio says it currently has a roughly 60% share of India's data traffic. In recent years, Jio Platforms has diversified beyond the telecom sector into AI, cloud and enterprise network services, as well as app development. In 2023, Nvidia (NVDA.O) announced an AI [USN:L1N3AK0MB TEXT:"partnership"] with Reliance to develop cloud infrastructure and language models. THE LEADERSHIP Mukesh Ambani, one of Asia's richest men, is the chairman of Jio Platforms. His three children — [USN:L4N4670YX TEXT:"Akash"], Anant and Isha — serve on its board. Akash Ambani, his elder son, is the chairman of the company's flagship telecom unit, Reliance Jio Infocomm. Pankaj Pawar is the CEO of Jio Platforms. KEY FINANCIALS, VALUATION Reliance Jio Platforms' revenue from operations rose 14.6% to 1.47 trillion rupees ($15.45 billion) in the fiscal year ended March, while profit increased 15.1% to 300.49 billion Indian rupees ($3.16 billion). Around 90% of those figures were attributable to its telecoms business alone. MARQUEE INVESTORS In 2020, Jio Platforms raised more than $20.5 billion from 13 global investors in exchange for a roughly 33% equity stake, at a valuation range of $57 billion to $65 billion. Global names such as Meta Platforms (META.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and KKR (KKR.N) invested in the firm, as Ambani sought to turn Jio Platforms into the centerpiece of his technology ambitions. Other investors include General Atlantic, Silver Lake and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority. Meta owns a 9.9% stake in the company, followed by Google's 7.7% stake. The Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock and Fidelity were among investors who bid in the anchor book of the IPO, which drew more than [USN:L4N4650J2 TEXT:"$25 billion in demand"]. THE IPO JOURNEY The filing, which had been targeted for as early as March, had been pushed back as IPO activity slowed following the outbreak of the Iran war, with investors losing their appetite for new listings. The company's shares started trading on October 28. It has been a long road to the IPO. In 2019, Ambani said Jio would "move towards" a listing within five years, and later the plans were delayed again in 2025. The company has hired [USN:L4N4060N2 TEXT:"19 banks"] to manage its offering.

item.title: Rays rally for 2 in 12th inning, extend World Series to Game 5
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- The Tampa Bay Rays were not going to be swept aside by rookie Cooper Pratt and the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- The Tampa Bay Rays were not going to be swept aside by rookie Cooper Pratt and the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday. Pinch hitter Ben Williamson delivered a walk-off single in the 12th inning as the Rays staved off elimination with a 4-3 victory over the Brewers on Tuesday in Game 4 of the World Series. The Brewers, who squandered a 12th-inning lead, still are up 3-1 in the best-of-seven series. Game 5 is set for Wednesday in St. Petersburg. "Gritty. Gritty. We're dangerous," Tampa Bay's Nick Martinez said. "We have our backs against the wall. ... We know what we have to do. We can win four in a row. This team is capable of doing that." After Pratt capped his four-hit performance with a homer to lead off the top of the 12th, giving Milwaukee a 3-2 lead, Tampa Bay saved its season with an epic rally in the bottom of the inning. Junior Caminero reached on a throwing error by third baseman Joey Ortiz to open the 12th inning and chase Antonio Senzatela from the game. "There's no excuse. Not one at all," Ortiz said. "I should make that play every f---- time." Shane Drohan (0-1) relieved Senzatela, and allowed a single to Liam Hicks to put runners on the corners. Jonny DeLuca's single up the middle plated pinch runner Cedric Mullins to forge a 3-3 tie. Chandler Simpson's single loaded the bases before Williamson bounced a chopper into right field, knocking in pinch runner Nick Fortes to end the game. Drohan, who was making his first relief appearance since Oct. 15, did not offer any excuses after the game. "(It's) definitely hard. I'm human, but I knew what I was walking into. I just didn't get the job done," said Drohan, who permitted one run on four hits without retiring a batter. Williamson had been 1-for-15 in the postseason before recording the game-winning hit. "You guys know how the game works, it's momentum, and we just got it right now," DeLuca told Fox Sports. "We're going to do everything we can to keep it going into tomorrow, We love the position we're in. We love being underdogs. We know the fight we have in this clubhouse, coaches, team, everyone. It's a fun position to be in." Brewers captain Christian Yelich believes his team will respond from this loss. "You're supposed to face adversity. You have to battle back from it. That's why you celebrate at the end, because that's what it requires out of you," he said. "I believe in our room and I believe we're prepared to meet that challenge." Pratt, who also had an RBI double in the fourth inning, deposited a 2-2 sweeper from Ian Seymour (2-0) over the wall in left-center field in the top of the 12th. Seymour allowed one run on two hits in one inning. Milwaukee's Jackson Chourio recorded two hits, boosting his total to 10 hits in the first four games of a World Series. The only other player to accomplish that feat was Babe Ruth in 1928. The Brewers' David Hamilton atoned for an earlier miscue by homering to lead off the fifth inning, tying the game 2-2. Simpson ripped an RBI double in the second inning and made a leaping catch at the wall in the ninth for the Rays, who (at least temporarily) prevented the Brewers from capturing their first World Series title. In the second, DeLuca reached on a fielder's choice and hustled home on Simpson's double into the right field corner to open the scoring. Sal Frelick reached on a two-out single and scampered home on Pratt's double into the left field corner to forge a 1-1 tie in the fourth inning. Tampa Bay answered in the bottom of the frame. Third baseman Hamilton's throw toward first base sailed off the mark, allowing Caminero to score from second and giving the Rays a 2-1 lead. In the fifth, Hamilton sent a 0-2 fastball from Griffin Jax over the wall in right center field to forge a 2-2 tie. The blast chased Jax from the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: China's CXMT to start advanced AI memory production despite poor yields, sources say
item.description: China's CXMT plans to start production of HBM3E, an advanced type of high-bandwidth memory chip used with AI processors, despite as little as 20% of the chips it makes being usable, two people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's CXMT plans to start production of HBM3E, an advanced type of high-bandwidth memory chip used with AI processors, despite as little as 20% of the chips it makes being usable, two people familiar with the matter said. The decision highlights China's [USN:L1N45902O TEXT:"intense shortage"] of the AI memory chips, which are essential to a government-backed push to develop domestic alternatives to Nvidia's (NVDA.O) AI processors at scale amid US curbs on access to foreign-made technology. ChangXin Memory Technologies (688825.SS) — China's largest maker of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), the conventional memory used in computers and servers — has sent HBM3E samples to several domestic AI chip designers, the people said. It expects to begin limited production over the next two months, one person said. Yields, or the share of chips coming off a production line that meet specifications, are only about 20% to 30%, compared with yields of around 70% at South Korea's SK Hynix (000660.KS) , the market leader, they said. The people declined to be identified because the plans are not public. CXMT did not respond to a request for comment. SK Hynix did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the yield estimate. The Information first reported CXMT's HBM3E plans. Reuters is reporting details about the product yields and delivery timeline for the first time. High-bandwidth memory (HBM) is made by vertically stacking memory chips so they can exchange data rapidly with AI processors. It is a crucial component in the specialized chips used to train and run large language models. Washington tightened export controls on certain advanced HBM products bound for China in December 2024. Chinese chipmakers have increasingly sought the memory through unofficial channels, where it can cost several times more, the people said. CXMT is pressing ahead despite low yields because Chinese AI chipmakers have struggled to obtain enough advanced memory to increase output, the people said. Low yields make production expensive because a large share of chips must be discarded or reworked. Reuters [USN:L1N45102L TEXT:"reported"] last month that Huawei [RIC:RIC:HWT.UL], Cambricon (688256.SS) , MetaX (688802.SS) and Iluvatar CoreX (9903.HK) had raised prices for current and next-generation AI chips by 20% to 50% as memory costs complicated efforts to ramp up production. CXMT's HBM3E is expected to cost more than comparable products from overseas rivals, one of the people said. The company began developing the technology internally as early as 2024, the people added. GENERATIONS BEHIND In testing, CXMT's HBM3E performance was closer to SK Hynix's previous-generation HBM3 than to the South Korean company's HBM3E, one of the people said. CXMT has sent customers two HBM3E versions, the other person said: a standard design and an updated version that includes changes intended to improve yields. The difficulty of producing HBM illustrates the gap between CXMT and the industry's established leaders — SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and Micron Technology (MU.O) — which dominate global supply. SK Hynix held 50% of global HBM revenue in the second quarter, according to Counterpoint Research, followed by Samsung with 33% and Micron with 18%. Most revenue came from HBM3E, the research firm said. CXMT held a 10% share of global DRAM revenue in the quarter, making it the world's fourth-largest supplier of conventional memory chips, Counterpoint said. But US export controls limit its access to some of the most advanced chipmaking equipment, making it harder to close the gap with global rivals. Samsung [USN:P8N41N01J TEXT:"said"] in July that it had expanded HBM4 sales and shipped HBM4E samples to major customers, putting CXMT at least one generation behind in commercial HBM production.

item.title: Boosting Western supply of refined critical metals means de-risking investment. But how?
item.description: The Western world is starting to reel in China's massive lead in producing and controlling the refined metals critical to defence, the transition to cleaner energy and the development of AI-related infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Clyde Russell
item.content:encoded: The Western world is starting to reel in China's massive lead in producing and controlling the refined metals critical to defence, the transition to cleaner energy and the development of AI-related infrastructure. The question is how to translate initial successes into a long-term, economically viable supply chain that bypasses the world's dominant producer. It was this question that dominated the International Mining and Resources Conference (IMARC) this week in Sydney, which brought together miners, governments and financiers to discuss how to turn the resource endowments of countries like [USN:L5N46D0DY TEXT:"Australia"] into refined metals. Unlike China, which can sustain forms of subsidies for state-controlled enterprises for years until economies of scale are achieved, Western nations are shaped more by finance and profitability. But it is also apparent that in a world where China dominates the production of refined metals and prices are often viewed as opaque, the previous model of mine development and downstream processing will not work. The United States is further ahead than the European Union in recognising that if critical minerals and metals are to be obtained in sufficient quantities and via relatively secure supply chains, then government intervention and support are going to be key. The traditional model of junior miners exploring and proving up a resource, then trying to raise capital to build a mine and eventually moving into production simply will not deliver the needed ore when compared with China's subsidy-driven rivals. And even if ore can be successfully mined, refining is often more challenging, especially in countries like Australia, with its high labour and energy costs and stringent environmental approvals. The main question at IMARC was how to significantly move the needle toward more secure supply for Western economies in a world where China controls 99% of the world's refined gallium, 74% of antimony, 81% of molybdenum, 91% of rare earths, 70% of lithium and 44% of copper, showed data from Visual Capitalist. And that is to name just a few of the vital metals. The answers were varied and reflected that no one tactic or policy is likely to deliver the necessary results. But there was some consensus on what measures are likely to bring the greatest chance of more rapid development of mineral resources. DE-RISKING The biggest factor is how to de-risk projects. Under the traditional model financing was only available if the developer could show that the cost of producing the minerals and metals would be less than the expected future price, or that offtake agreements were in place that guaranteed revenue. It was on this basis that Australia was able to approve massive resource expansion, such as Japanese investment into coal and iron ore mines, and both Japanese and Chinese support for liquefied natural gas projects. Australia also jumped in the past decade to become the world's largest lithium producer, but this was achieved largely with Chinese money and the vast majority of the country's mined lithium ore is processed in China for use by Chinese vehicle and battery manufacturers. For more minor metals with opaque pricing the situation is more complex. There are three main tactics to try and speed up development. The first is to set a floor price for the commodity, as the United States has done for the rare earth compound neodymium-praseodymium, which is used to make magnets. The minimum price of $110 per kilogram gives producers certainty and may end up costing US taxpayers nothing as the price of the compound has risen to trade above the floor. The second is to guarantee offtake, giving producers confidence that buyers will be available for the product at prices that will ensure viability, even if those prices are higher than what is charged by Chinese-controlled suppliers. The third is to directly invest in mines and downstream processing and be prepared to subsidise losses until economic viability can be achieved. The trick is in working out which tactic will deliver the best outcome, and this is likely to vary from project to project. For metals where the government is the main buyer, such as those used by defence industries, owning stakes may be the answer. For industries vital to technology and the energy transition, setting minimum prices and ensuring offtake agreements are likely the better solution. What is lacking so far is a comprehensive strategy across the developed Western economies, and at IMARC it was also clear that the United States and the European Union are showing signs of competing with each other, rather than working together. The risk is that the Western response to China's dominance of refined critical metals remains fragmented and uncoordinated. Enjoying this column?
