item.title: NBA roundup: Jayson Tatum's OT buzzer-beater lifts Celtics over Nets
item.description: Jayson Tatum made an elbow jumper as time expired in overtime to give the Boston Celtics a 125-124 victory over the visiting Brooklyn Nets on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jayson Tatum made an elbow jumper as time expired in overtime to give the Boston Celtics a 125-124 victory over the visiting Brooklyn Nets on Tuesday night. Tatum scored a game-high 40 points and hit a career-high 18 free throws on 22 attempts. Paul George added 20 points, seven rebounds and seven assists for Boston, which won its third game in a row. Michael Porter Jr. amassed 27 points and 12 rebounds for the Nets, who fell to 0-4. Julius Randle finished with 24 points and nine rebounds. Brooklyn trailed 117-114 late in the fourth quarter, but Mikel Brown Jr. sent the game to overtime by making a 3-pointer with one second left. Knicks 111, Pistons 97 Karl-Anthony Towns scored 13 of his game-high 27 points during a decisive third-quarter run as host New York rallied past Detroit for its first win of the season. The Knicks outscored the Pistons 37-13 in the third and held off a fourth-quarter rally to avoid becoming the first defending NBA champion to open 0-4 since the Boston Celtics in 1969-70. Towns also pulled down a season-high 20 rebounds, while Jalen Brunson produced 23 points and seven assists. Paul Reed had 22 points and nine rebounds for the Pistons, who were seeking their first 4-0 start since the 2018-19 season. Cade Cunningham totaled 19 points, nine rebounds and eight assists. Spurs 130, Kings 103 Victor Wembanyama poured in 29 points and grabbed 10 rebounds in just 27 minutes, and Julian Champagnie canned eight first-half 3-pointers as host San Antonio steamrolled Sacramento. San Antonio set league season highs for points (80), assists (23) and 3-pointers (13) in a half in a near-complete performance before the break. Champagnie finished with 26 points as the Spurs won their second game in a row. De'Andre Hunter put up 24 points for the Kings, who dropped to 0-4 on the season. Zach LaVine added 22, and Domantas Sabonis amassed 20 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists. --Field Level Media

item.title: Morning Bid: RBNZ throws markets a curveball
item.description: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rae Wee
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rae Wee The shocker in Asia's trading day came from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, which [USN:L6N46E02E TEXT:"unexpectedly left rates on hold"], sending the kiwi sliding. The decision was by a narrow vote and came with agreement that tighter policy is necessary. But according to Westpac, it's the first time outside the pandemic that the central bank held rates while markets had priced a [USN:L2N46E01K TEXT:"more than 70% chance"] of a hike. The New Zealand dollar tumbled more than 1%, and the news sent the Aussie jumping 2% against its Antipodean counterpart to its highest in 13 years. Wednesday's RBNZ decision kicks off a slew of [USN:L6N45N0UX TEXT:"central bank policy announcements"], with the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Canada set to follow later in the day. The Fed is widely expected to keep rates on hold, while the BoC is [USN:L6N46911N TEXT:"seen hiking"] by 25 basis points, though that could potentially change. If anything, the RBNZ's decision suggests policymakers may be comfortable with playing the waiting game, and that markets may have gotten ahead of themselves in pricing in rate hikes globally. As Commonwealth Bank of Australia's Carol Kong puts it: "Today's decision shows the RBNZ is willing to surprise markets, a reminder that central banks do not take orders from markets." Down Under, [USN:L2N46E00K TEXT:"Australia's inflation"] picked up in the third quarter on higher fuel costs, while stubbornly hot underlying price pressures cemented market expectations of a fifth interest rate hike as soon as next week. South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix (000660.KS) announced [USN:L2N46D1DE TEXT:"shareholder returns"] of about $75 billion on Wednesday, after reporting a more than sevenfold rise in quarterly profit as AI infrastructure continues to drive up memory chip prices. The upbeat results kept [USN:L2N46E012 TEXT:"stocks in Asia"] well supported, with much now riding on earnings from [USN:L3N46D1FP TEXT:"technology giants"] Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Microsoft (MSFT.O) to sustain the momentum. Investors are pressing for evidence that the AI boom can deliver swift returns to justify its enormous price tag. Rising bond yields at AI cloud providers such as CoreWeave (CRWV.O) and record costs to insure Meta Platforms' (META.O) debt have amplified concerns about how the massive AI infrastructure buildout is being funded, particularly as higher US interest rates loom. Meanwhile, Israel's [USN:L2N46D04I TEXT:"wartime election"] appeared deadlocked, exit polls showed, with Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc running neck and neck with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp, leaving neither side with a clear path to power. Key developments that could influence markets on Wednesday: - Federal Reserve rate decision - Bank of Canada rate decision - Alphabet, Microsoft earnings

item.title: China dismisses Taiwan's accusations of involvement in comedian attack
item.description: Taiwan is "provoking confrontation" and stirring anti-China sentiment, a Chinese government spokesperson said on Wednesday, after Taiwanese prosecutors indicted five people for plotting to attack a Taiwanese comedian whose shows mocked Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Taiwan is "provoking confrontation" and stirring anti-China sentiment, a Chinese government spokesperson said on Wednesday, after Taiwanese prosecutors indicted five people for plotting to attack a Taiwanese [USN:L4N4670DY TEXT:"comedian"] whose shows mocked Beijing. Taiwan, the democratically governed island that China claims as its own territory, has accused Beijing of trying to use "transnational repression" against people in Taiwan the Chinese government views as separatists or politically suspect. Taiwan's government says China was behind last month's attack on comedian Huang Yi-hao, who satirised Chinese President Xi Jinping. Speaking at a regular news conference in Beijing and asked about the incident, Taiwan Affairs Office spokesperson Chen Binhua dismissed Taiwan's accusations as a fabrication by its ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP). "The so-called transnational repression narrative is essentially a way of promoting Taiwan independence and peddling a two-state theory, and it is trotted out every time there is an election on the island," he said, referring to next month's local elections in Taiwan. "The DPP fabricates all kinds of pretexts out of thin air, maliciously smears the mainland, stirs up anti-China sentiment, and provokes cross-strait confrontation, all in an attempt to win political power by misleading the Taiwanese public," Chen said. This is a "tired routine" repeated year after year, he added. Taiwan prosecutors said the defendants, whose full names it has not provided, were paid to fake a car accident and "break the arms and legs" of Huang so he could not perform, though in the end he was only lightly injured. Taiwan Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung, in a report delivered to lawmakers earlier on Wednesday, said the case of Huang and others showed what he described as China's expanding efforts to "challenge people's personal safety, freedom of expression, and the resilience of democratic society." Other China critics in Taiwan have also been attacked, including [USN:KBN1WE0L8 TEXT:"Hong Kong singer and activist Denise Ho"] in 2019. Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, saying only the Taiwanese people can decide their future.

item.title: Unilever India posts higher profit on healthy demand
item.description: Consumer goods maker Hindustan Unilever reported a 6% rise in quarterly profit on Wednesday, as healthy demand cushioned the blow from higher raw material costs.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Consumer goods maker Hindustan Unilever (HLL.NS) reported a 6% rise in quarterly profit on Wednesday, as healthy demand cushioned the blow from higher raw material costs. The Indian arm of the UK's Unilever (ULVR.L) , home to brands such as Pepsodent and Dove, said it made a profit of 28.44 billion rupees ($299.01 million) for the quarter ended September 30, compared to 26.9 billion rupees a year earlier. Indian consumer goods makers are seeking to drive growth through wider distribution, more premium products, as well as raising prices to counter higher costs of commodities such as sugar, edible oils and crude oil. For Hindustan Unilever, product sales climbed 15% to 173.99 billion rupees, with volume growing 7% in the quarter through September 30. "Indian economy remains resilient, with healthy macro indicators supporting a positive consumption environment," said CEO and Managing Director Priya Nair. ($1 = 95.1150 Indian rupees)

item.title: StanChart lifts full-year targets after quarterly profit trounces forecasts
item.description: Standard Chartered (StanChart) on Wednesday hiked its income and profitability targets after third-quarter profit handily beat estimates with robust performances from its wealth and global markets divisions.
item.dc:creator: Selena Li, Lawrence White
item.content:encoded: Standard Chartered (StanChart) (STAN.L) on Wednesday hiked its income and profitability targets after third-quarter profit handily beat estimates with robust performances from its wealth and global markets divisions. It lifted its full-year income growth target for 2026 to above 7% from its earlier estimate in the middle of a 5-7% range. And it also boosted its return on tangible equity target, a key performance gauge, to above 14% from an earlier forecast of exceeding 12%. The bank's Hong Kong-listed shares extended gains to be up 5.4% after the results. StanChart, which earns most of its revenue in Asia and Africa, said pretax profit for the July-September quarter surged 27% to $2.25 billion, ahead of a consensus of $1.99 billion drawn from analyst estimates compiled by the bank. Like European peers, StanChart has had a run of strong performances, but its guidance for returns of 14% in 2026 versus the 17% expected by rival HSBC (HSBA.L) shows StanChart still has room to improve. StanChart's wealth division delivered a third consecutive record quarter, with income up 26%, supported by broad-based momentum across products and geographies, the bank said. The bank has accelerated its wealth expansion plan, aiming to gain net new money inflows of $200 billion between 2025 and 2028, ahead of its original 2029 target. Its fee-based revenue, less sensitive to rate changes, surged 19% to $2.81 billion in the quarter from a year earlier, ahead of an average estimate of $2.68 billion.

item.title: France minerals envoy says rare earths diversification from China possible within 3-5 years
item.description: Western countries could achieve an acceptable level of rare earths diversification away from China within three to five years, France's top envoy for strategic metals said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Melanie Burton
item.content:encoded: Western countries could achieve an acceptable level of rare earths diversification away from China within three to five years, France's top envoy for strategic metals said on Wednesday. Governments and manufacturers are racing to diversify supplies of metals vital to defence, technology and renewable energy and reduce dependence on China which accounts for as much as 90% of production of some specialised rare earth magnets. Beijing rattled global markets last year when export curbs on permanent magnets disrupted industries, including the automotive sector, exposing their reliance on a single source. Some investors and analysts have questioned whether breaking China's dominance is achievable, given the scale of investment and technical know-how required to produce the niche metals used in everything from cars and aircraft to electronics and weapons systems. "You don't need hundreds of rare earths mines around the world to cover the supply. It's a limited market, it's a limited quantity. We have already made some progress," said Benjamin Gallezot, France's Interministerial Delegate for Strategic Minerals and Metals Supply. Expansion projects led by Belgium's Solvay (SOLB.BR) and France's Carester, plus others in Australia, the US, Japan, Brazil, and India are developing quickly, he said. "If you take all together, these projects, and you push to accelerate them, hopefully you can have a good diversification in the next three to five years," he said, speaking on the sidelines of a mining conference in Sydney. While rare earths mines and refining projects were progressing, the amount of magnet manufacturing could still be a limiting factor, he said. "You don't need a decade to solve this problem." Leaders of the Group of Seven nations agreed in June to step up [USN:L6N42P0XG TEXT:"coordination"] to cut their countries' reliance on China for critical minerals. They aim to reduce dependence on any one supplier outside the G7 and its partner countries for rare earths and permanent magnets to below 60% by 2030, with an ultimate goal of 50% "as soon as possible". "We can do much more," Gallezot said.

item.title: China's aluminium producers push abroad as domestic growth hits ceiling
item.description: Chinese aluminium producers are pushing abroad as part of an expansion spree that could tip the world market for the metal into surplus even as the wave of investment faces greater scrutiny from Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Duan, Lewis Jackson
item.content:encoded: Chinese aluminium producers are pushing abroad as part of an expansion spree that could tip the world market for the metal into surplus even as the wave of investment faces greater scrutiny from Beijing. At least 15 million metric tons a year of primary aluminium smelting capacity is planned or has been announced by Chinese investors across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Central Asia and Africa, a Reuters review of company disclosures and government filings showed. About 2.85 million tons a year of that is ramping up or under construction, the review showed, equal to 3.8% of current global annual capacity of 73.78 million tons. The new near-term smelter projects, along with recovering Middle East output, will help swing the global aluminium market from a 1.1 million-ton deficit this year to an 830,000-ton surplus next year and a 1.8-million-ton surplus in 2028, Morgan Stanley (MS.N) [USN:L4N43B0SU TEXT:"forecast"] in July. Chinese aluminium producers are looking overseas for growth because domestic smelting capacity is capped at 45 million tons a year under a policy introduced in 2017 to curb overcapacity and pollution. How much of the planned capacity will ultimately be built is unclear, as new supply could lower prices and put projects further down the pipeline at risk. Also, Beijing is increasing its scrutiny of outbound direct investments by Chinese companies and access to power overseas remains an impediment to new plants. "Ultimately, it comes down to economics. Most of these companies are privately owned and profit-driven," said Rachel Zhang, head of China materials research at Morgan Stanley. "If a project clearly does not make money, why would they invest in it?" The expected additions should weigh on metal prices. Morgan Stanley has cut its average price forecast in 2027 to $2,850 a ton and for 2028 to $2,800. It expects aluminium to average $3,150 in the second half of 2026. Benchmark three-month aluminium prices on the London Metal Exchange were at $3,097.50 a ton as of 0300 GMT on Wednesday. Chinese metal demand for manufacturing and electric vehicles that exceeds the domestic capacity cap is driving the overseas expansion as well as the companies' outlook for rising consumption as much as 20 years ahead, said Andrew Denton, research director at metals industry analytics company AME Group in Sydney. "These projects would have to be predicated on a much longer-term view of demand growth for primary aluminium, which we see," he said. "The broader themes for demand with electrification and EVs for aluminium are positive." INDONESIA FIRST Indonesia, which has attracted tens of billions of dollars in Chinese nickel investment, has emerged as a major destination for Chinese aluminium investment. Zhang at Morgan Stanley expects Indonesia to add 866,000 tons of annual smelting capacity in 2026 and another 1.2 million to 1.3 million tons in 2027. The projects include Shandong Nanshan Aluminium's 250,000-ton-per-year facility on the island of Bintan that is under construction, with an expansion that would double capacity planned as well. In Central Sulawesi's Morowali Industrial Park, Xinfa Group and Tsingshan Holding Group are commissioning a facility with a capacity of 600,000 tons per year. Tsingshan is also working on a new facility at the existing smelting hub of Weda Bay in North Maluku province of 800,000 tons per year. Beyond Indonesia, Chinese projects in Kazakhstan and Saudi Arabia would add around 4 million tons a year of capacity. In Saudi Arabia, Shandong Innovation Group-backed Red Sea Aluminium is building a 500,000-ton-a-year smelter in Yanbu, targeting production in 2027. The project reached preliminary partnership terms with the kingdom's Public Investment Fund in January. In Kazakhstan, Xinfa is pursuing a 2.4-million-ton-a-year smelter in Pavlodar, among the largest projects in the pipeline. Globally, Morgan Stanley expects around 2.1 million tons of new annual capacity in 2027 and 2.2 million tons in 2028. SCRUTINY IN BEIJING Still, global prices and Chinese oversight will decide how much is built. Overseas aluminium deals face stricter regulatory scrutiny under [USN:P8N40T00Z TEXT:"new outbound investment rules"] that started in July, according to two sources briefed by some of the Chinese companies that are moving overseas. The rules allow authorities to review overseas investments on national security grounds and order companies to halt projects or divest assets. In October, Fan Shunke, the deputy party secretary of the state-backed China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association, said a huge expansion overseas was not desirable nor feasible. While large integrated projects are still likely to go ahead, though with more delays, the new rules will make it more difficult for smaller stand-alone smelters, according to Alan Clark, Adelaide-based founder of aluminium consultancy CM Group, who has spent more than two decades researching China's metals industry. Of the 15 million tons of new capacity identified by Reuters, Clark estimates that only between 9 million and 10 million tons will eventually be built, about half of that in Indonesia.

item.title: AI worries expose dollar's hot-money problem
item.description: Investors have long treated the US dollar as a refuge when markets fall, but foreign money chasing returns from the AI boom could weaken that safe-haven role if the trade unwinds.
item.dc:creator: Karen Brettell
item.content:encoded: Investors have long treated the US dollar as a refuge when markets fall, but foreign money chasing returns from the AI boom could weaken that safe-haven role if the trade unwinds. Foreign capital has poured in to US mega-cap equities, hyperscaler corporate bonds and power-grid infrastructure. That has made the dollar an increasingly crowded bet on American exceptionalism, backed by faster growth, higher yields and persistent foreign demand for US assets. But if the AI narrative stumbles, the dollar's safe-haven status could collide with its growing role as a risk-sensitive asset owned increasingly by price-sensitive investors. A sustained selloff in stocks could lead investors to sell US assets, potentially drowning out the safe-haven demand for the currency. If the AI trade unwinds, "it's not as clear the dollar benefits in the same way it would have done in the past," said Dominic Bunning, head of G10 FX strategy at Nomura. STORM WARNING ON FOREX FLOWS Last week [USN:L6N4681D7 TEXT:"offered an early warning"]. When AI valuations came under pressure, haven flows favored the Japanese yen and Swiss franc over the dollar. The greenback managed to eke out modest gains against the euro, mainly due to the single currency being dented by concerns over French civil unrest. "The relationship between the AI trade and the dollar has become much more visible when the AI trade comes under scrutiny," said Kevin Ford, lead FX and macro strategist at Convera. Foreign flows into US equities are at a record, while foreign direct investment has lagged. As a result, much of the capital is coming from institutional allocators that may buy or sell when they reassess US growth, rates, or tech valuations. Erik Nelson, global head of FX strategy at Wells Fargo, likens these allocations to the "hot money" flows that dominate emerging markets. The AI boom has reinforced expectations of stronger US growth, firmer inflation and higher rates, lifting the dollar alongside Treasury yields, analysts said. "The whole AI trade caused US rates to reprice higher, which has caused the dollar to rally," said Noah Buffam, FX strategist at CIBC Capital Markets. If returns disappoint, an unwind could hit equities, credit and rates, leaving the dollar vulnerable on three fronts. Weaker growth could force the Federal Reserve to cut rates, eroding the dollar's yield advantage. Slower domestic investment would puncture the exceptionalism narrative. And fading institutional demand for US corporate bonds and equities would weaken a major source of structural support. So far, investors have been willing to buy dips, suggesting that any sustained weakness could be a process taking months or years. THE DOTCOM LESSON An equity rout alone would not automatically sink the dollar, Nelson said. After the Nasdaq peaked in March 2000, the dollar stayed firm for nearly two years before cracking when US credit markets came under stress following collapses such as WorldCom's, and due to other factors such as a recovery in global growth. But the AI buildout is more US-centric. Nelson said the real trade-weighted dollar has stayed above its long-run average, measured since 1973, for 12 consecutive years, the longest stretch on record. Foreign inflows are also more concentrated in equities and corporate bonds than in 2000, while foreign direct investment is weaker. If infrastructure investments fail to pay off, credit spreads could widen, forcing AI companies to curb capital spending. That could ripple through the economy, softening demand for industrial equipment, hardware and energy. Concerns about riskier parts of the AI universe, such as heavily indebted neocloud companies [USN:L4N461208 TEXT:"including CoreWeave"] (CRWV.O) , have already widened credit default swap spreads sharply in recent weeks, adding to pressure on stocks. "We can see this fraying around the edges when we look at credit default swaps," said Shaun Osborne, chief FX strategist at Scotiabank. Washington also runs a large fiscal deficit now, compared with a surplus near the 2000 tech peak. That leaves less room for counter-cyclical stimulus without unsettling debt markets. SENSITIVITY UNDER STRESS For Nelson, the key signal is not simply whether US tech shares fall, but whether stress becomes a US-specific credit and growth problem that can also change expectations for Fed policy. In such a scenario the yen would likely benefit at the dollar's expense, a shift that could have further ramifications for markets that would already likely be under stress. That is not to say a dollar decline is a foregone conclusion. A shock severe enough to trigger a scramble for dollar funding could initially strengthen the dollar. In 2008 and March 2020, investors rushed to obtain dollars to meet dollar-denominated liabilities, creating a powerful but temporary bid. In any case, some investors believe the dollar is back on the table as a major risk factor in the most significant way since the rout caused by US President Donald Trump 's announcement of sweeping tariffs in April 2025. "The sensitivity of global investors to a large re-rating or selloff in the dollar is substantial," Nelson said. "As we go into '27, it's a vulnerability for the dollar that I think is worth watching.”

item.title: India's L&T jumps as quarterly profit beat eases Middle East concerns
item.description: Shares of India's Larsen & Toubro rose more than 6% in early trading on Wednesday after the engineering conglomerate posted a 33% jump in second-quarter profit, driven by strong order inflows and easing concerns over Middle East project execution.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shares of India's Larsen & Toubro rose more than 6% in early trading on Wednesday after the engineering conglomerate posted a 33% jump in second-quarter profit, driven by strong order inflows and easing concerns over Middle East project execution. The stock was up 4.38% at 3,826.10 rupees, as of 9:35 a.m. IST. L&T, seen as a barometer for India's infrastructure sector, [USN:L3N46D162 TEXT:"reported"] a profit of 52.02 billion rupees ($546.92 million) in July-September on Tuesday, while revenue rose 16% to 787.5 billion rupees. Order inflows rose 28% to 1.48 trillion rupees in the reported quarter, taking the company's outstanding order book to a record 8.54 trillion rupees. International orders accounted for 63% of new orders. J.P. Morgan said L&T's strong execution, despite the ongoing Middle East conflict, eased concerns about its ability to meet annual growth targets, noting that projects in the region continued despite logistical challenges. The brokerage maintained its "Overweight" rating but lowered its price target to 4,960 rupees from 5,060 rupees, citing higher logistics costs affecting solar projects in the Middle East. Investec raised its profit estimates for fiscal 2027 through 2029 by 3%-4% on stronger-than-expected revenue growth, healthy order inflows and improved working capital. It maintained its "Buy" rating and raised its price target to 5,000 rupees from 4,870 rupees. Jefferies also maintained its "Buy" rating, citing L&T's strong order book and execution, but cut its price target to 4,700 rupees from 5,000 rupees to account for weaker engineering and construction margins. L&T maintained its fiscal 2027 guidance for revenue and order inflow growth of 10%-12% each, despite geopolitical tensions affecting some projects in the Middle East. ($1 = 95.1150 Indian rupees)

item.title: India's Bajaj Auto gains as export strength, EV growth drive earnings beat
item.description: Shares of India's Bajaj Auto rose as much as 3.1% on Wednesday after the motorcycle maker's quarterly profit beat estimates, reinforcing expectations that strong export demand and rapid growth in its electric-vehicle business will drive its next phase of expansion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shares of India's Bajaj Auto (BAJA.NS) rose as much as 3.1% on Wednesday after the motorcycle maker's quarterly profit beat estimates, reinforcing expectations that strong export demand and rapid growth in its electric-vehicle business will drive its next phase of expansion. The stock was up 2% at 10,600 rupees as of 10:17 a.m. IST. The Nifty Auto index was up 0.3%, while the benchmark Nifty 50 index was down 1%. Bajaj, which makes the Pulsar motorcycles and electric Chetak two-wheeler, reported a 35.3% rise in second-quarter profit while revenue from operations rose 34.1%. Export volumes jumped 41%, outpacing growth in its domestic two-wheeler business. Exports and EVs are emerging as Bajaj Auto's twin growth engines, helping offset cost pressures and boost investor confidence in its earnings momentum, analysts said. The company said its EV business accounted for nearly 35% of domestic revenue in the quarter. It plans to raise monthly Chetak production capacity to about 80,000 units by the fourth quarter from 60,000-65,000 currently. Citi said sustained export momentum and festive demand supported its growth outlook, while CLSA said higher Chetak capacity, refreshed Pulsar models and two planned motorcycle brands could help Bajaj gain market share. CLSA retained its "outperform" rating and raised its fiscal 2027 and 2028 earnings estimates by 4%. Analysts also highlighted strong realisations from favourable currency movements. Morgan Stanley said the company's EBITDA margin beat its estimates, aided by foreign-exchange gains, production-linked incentives and a more favourable export mix. EV capacity additions and planned launches supported the growth outlook, it added, but retained its "underweight" rating, citing risks to sustaining current margins amid elevated commodity costs.

item.title: Indonesia beefs up security presence to prepare for student protests
item.description: Hundreds of Indonesian security personnel were deployed on Wednesday in anticipation of student protests against several of President Prabowo Subianto's policies, as well as his government's handling of forest fires.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hundreds of Indonesian security personnel were deployed on Wednesday in anticipation of student protests against several of President Prabowo Subianto's policies, as well as his government's handling of forest fires. Students from the University of Indonesia said they were set to stage protests in several spots in the capital Jakarta They are calling on the government to declare the ongoing wildfires in Sumatra and Borneo a national disaster, and to halt spending on populist programmes such as Prabowo's [USN:L1N4530A5 TEXT:"free meals scheme"], among other demands Wednesday's protests carry the hashtag #IndonesiaAware, the students said It is unclear how many students will take to the streets A heavy police and military presence, as well as armoured vehicles, could be seen in busy parts of central Jakarta on Wednesday morning Protests have also been held in haze-stricken areas of Borneo and Sumatra, including one in [USN:L6N46C0K9 TEXT:"Central Kalimantan"] last week Prabowo's approval ratings have fallen steadily since late last year, according to surveys by Saiful Mujani Research and Consulting (SMRC), two years into his presidency Indonesia's last major protest took place in August, when [USN:L1N44P0CI TEXT:"hundreds"] were detained, and students also held demonstrations [USN:L6N46606S TEXT:"last week"] In 2025, weeks-long nationwide protests broke out in Indonesia after the police killing of a motorcycle taxi driver, with several more people killed during the unrest

item.title: Anthropic offers glimmer of hope for China AI labs
item.description: The US titan's disclosures reveal first-half revenue hit $16 bln, growing faster than Z.AI and MiniMax, and confirms frontier-model investment can pay off. But while the Chinese duo's sales lag Anthropic's by only two years each, they may struggle to match its pricing power.
item.dc:creator: Robyn Mak
item.content:encoded: Anthropic's IPO filing is drawing intense scrutiny from global investors and Chinese rivals alike. The US titan's first-half revenue hit $16 billion, growing faster than Z.AI (2513.HK) and MiniMax (0100.HK) , and its financials show that investing in frontier artificial intelligence models can pay off. But while the listed Chinese duo's sales lag Anthropic's by only two years each, the real gap may be much larger. The company co-founded and led by Dario Amodei has revealed formidable strengths. The first is size: Anthropic's top line for the six months to the end of June is 63 times Z.AI and MiniMax's combined showing in the same period. Their American rival benefits from a rapidly expanding and mostly US-based pool of enterprises paying as much as $10 million a year to use its Claude family of models. Heady growth puts the US company on a path to shoring up its bottom line too. Anthropic is still splurging on computing power and infrastructure to deploy and train large language models - those costs nearly quadrupled year-on-year to $8.9 billion in the first six months of 2026. But it is benefiting from hardware and software efficiencies and generating more revenue per dollar of compute. It turned an operating profit of $1.6 billion in the period, albeit on an adjusted basis. By contrast, Chinese AI labs, hobbled by US chip export controls, have a long way to go. Their skimpy revenue partly reflects that their models are free to download. They only charge users for access and customisations - and at ultra-low prices. That has resulted in [USN:L6N44V0A3 TEXT:"brutal economics"]: the cost of training competitive models, as reflected in research and development expenses, dwarfs each of MiniMax and Z.AI's top lines. Z.AI's annualised first-half 2026 revenue of $284 million puts it roughly where Anthropic was in 2024, when the US firm generated just $386 million in sales. MiniMax is in a similar position. But factor in slow enterprise adoption in China, alongside fierce domestic competition, and it is suddenly hard to see Z.AI or MiniMax commanding Anthropic's pricing power for their models and agents. Z.AI's flagship GLM 5.2 model is widely considered frontier-level and costs on average nearly a third less to use than Claude Opus 5.5, per Artificial Analysis . Sure, Anthropic's finances will look different as soon as it plans "substantial capital expenditures" to secure its own compute. For now, its performance is highlighting the gap between US and China AI companies. Follow Robyn Mak on X . Anthropic reported revenue in the six months to June 30 of $16.3 billion, up from $1.2 billion a year earlier, per the company's US IPO filing released on October 26. Adjusted operating income for the period was $1.6 billion. Since 2025, the company reclassified its operating expenses based on the nature of expenses, such as compute and infrastructure, personnel, sales, marketing and partnerships and others. Compute and infrastructure, primarily costs from research and model development and serving customers, rose to $8.9 billion in the first half, up from $2.3 billion last year. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: US judge narrows French President Macron's defamation lawsuit against podcaster
item.description: A judge in Delaware ruled on Tuesday that French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife, Brigitte, could continue their defamation lawsuit against the companies of right-wing podcaster Candace Owens, but not against Owens herself.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A judge in Delaware ruled on Tuesday that French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife, Brigitte, could continue their defamation lawsuit against the companies of right-wing podcaster Candace Owens, but not against Owens herself. [USN:L1N3TK0R0 TEXT:"The Macrons sued Owens"] and two Delaware-registered businesses associated with her in July over what they called her lie-filled "campaign of global humiliation", including the claim that France's first lady was born a male Superior Court Judge Sheldon Rennie agreed in a Tuesday order that his court did not have jurisdiction over Owens, who lives in Tennessee, but the defamation case against the businesses, Candace Owens LLC and Georgetom Inc, could continue for now as they were registered in Delaware Rennie deferred judgment on Owens' motion to dismiss the Macrons' litigation until the parties had briefed him further on how French defamation law and statutes of limitation intersect with US law Owens thanked the judge in a social media statement, saying the case "represents one of the grossest, legal overreaches by a foreign government leader in human history — a sitting President's attempt to personally bankrupt a single podcaster from outside the nation in which he governs" In their lawsuit, the Macrons said Owens touted false claims and conspiracy theories against them "to promote her independent platform, gain notoriety, and make money"

item.title: Australia's Star Entertainment fined $183 million for anti-money laundering law breaches
item.description: An Australian federal court on Wednesday fined casino operator Star Entertainment A$260 million ($182.73 million) for breaching anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing laws, according to a court judgment.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An Australian federal court on Wednesday fined casino operator Star Entertainment (SGR.AX) A$260 million ($182.73 million) for breaching anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing laws, according to a court judgment. The penalty stems from a civil lawsuit brought in 2022 by the Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre (AUSTRAC), which alleged Star entities failed to comply with anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing regulations. The fine is lower than the roughly A$400 million penalty sought by the financial crime watchdog, according to media reports last year. The court found that Star Sydney's anti-money laundering program failed to meet legal requirements and breached the law on multiple occasions each time it began providing designated services to customers between November 30, 2016, and November 30, 2022, among other violations. The casino operator reported earlier this week that it had [USN:L3N46D076 TEXT:"A$239 million in cash and cash equivalents"] at the end of last month and A$80 million in restricted deposits. Star shares were placed on a trading halt earlier on Wednesday ahead of the court's decision in the AUSTRAC case. AUSTRAC did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. ($1 = 1.4229 Australian dollars)

item.title: Jacob Fowler's career-high 46 saves help Canadiens blank Blues
item.description: Jacob Fowler made a career-high 46 saves for the shutout in the Montreal Canadiens' 2-0 road win over the St. Louis Blues on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jacob Fowler made a career-high 46 saves for the shutout in the Montreal Canadiens' 2-0 road win over the St. Louis Blues on Tuesday. The Canadiens are on a three-game winning streak, all on the road. The Habs are on a five-game (4-0-1) points streak and are 6-1-1 in their last eight games. St. Louis outshot Montreal by a 46-20 margin, including a whopping 24-3 edge in the third period. Despite all the pressure, the Blues couldn't solve Fowler in the goaltender's latest sensational performance. Fowler has two shutouts over the course of a six-game winning streak, plus a .942 save percentage in his seven total games this season. Since the 1955-56 season, only 25 Montreal goalies have recorded more than 46 saves in a regular-season game. Zack Bolduc and Florian Xhekaj scored for the Habs, and Mike Matheson had two assists. The Blues are on a two-game losing streak and goal-less streak, as the Carolina Hurricanes also blanked St. Louis by a 4-0 score on Saturday. Jordan Binnington stopped 18 of 20 shots. Philip Broberg led the Blues with six shots against Fowler. Jake Neighbours had five shots and perhaps the closest call of the game, as Neighbours rang a shot off the goalpost 13:20 into the first period. The Habs opened the scoring 8:37 into the second period when Matheson sent a tremendous pass to Bolduc for a one-timer from the front edge of the circle. Bolduc's goal came three seconds after a Montreal power play expired, so the Canadiens officially went 0-for-3 with the extra attacker on Tuesday. The Habs' struggling power-play unit is only 4-for-35 in 12 games. At the 2:17 mark of the third period, Xhekaj's first NHL goal had to be confirmed by a video review. Xhekaj's tip-in of a Matheson shot was ruled to not be a high stick, giving Xhekaj his milestone in his ninth career NHL game. Binnington spent most of the last seven minutes on the bench, as St. Louis coach Jim Montgomery pulled his goalie unusually early in the third period. This extended 6-on-5 stretch contributed to the Blues' 24-3 shots advantage in the third period, yet Fowler held his ground and the Canadiens were continually able to ice the puck. --Field Level Media

item.title: Predators rally from 3-goal hole, but Islanders prevail in shootout
item.description: The New York Islanders surrendered a three-goal, second-period lead but went on to win in a shootout, beating the host Nashville Predators 4-3 on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The New York Islanders surrendered a three-goal, second-period lead but went on to win in a shootout, beating the host Nashville Predators 4-3 on Tuesday. Anthony Duclair, Brayden Schenn and Bo Horvat scored in regulation for the Islanders. Kyle Palmieri and Horvat tallied in the shootout. Semyon Varlamov made 20 saves for New York, which had lost its other two games that went past regulation. In his first NHL victory since November 2024, Varlamov also poke-checked the puck away from Nashville's Ryan O'Reilly to open the shootout. Filip Forsberg had a goal and an assist for the Predators, who earned at least a point in their third straight game (1-0-2). Alexander Kerfoot and O'Reilly also scored. Juuse Saros stopped 25 shots in defeat. The Islanders controlled the first period, outshooting Nashville 9-6 and scoring twice in a five-minute span. Duclair scored his third goal of the season during a 4-on-4 stretch with 16:53 remaining in the opening period. From the low slot, he redirected Jean-Gabriel Pageau's crossing pass from the boards. Schenn doubled the Islanders' lead with 11:53 remaining in the first, scoring on a second effort. His fourth goal of the season came off a pass from Ondrej Palat to the net. Horvat made it 3-0 just 68 seconds into the second period with a one-timer off a pass from Matthew Schaefer. It was Horvat's team-high sixth goal, and Schaefer recorded his team-leading ninth assist. Simon Holmstrom also helped set up the play. Nashville finally got on the board midway through the second on a power play after Schenn was called for hooking. Forsberg scored his third goal of the season and second in as many games, with assists from Jonathan Marchessault and Steven Stamkos. The Predators pulled within one with 6:58 remaining in the second when Kerfoot took the puck away in the Islanders' zone and eventually put in a rebound off Nils Hoglander's second shot on goal. O'Reilly tied the game with 15:44 remaining in regulation, just 21 seconds after leaving the penalty box, putting home a loose rebound off a shot by Daemon Hunt. The Islanders controlled most of the five-minute overtime, aided by a tripping penalty against Forsberg. Forsberg then shot wide on Nashville's second attempt in the shootout, allowing Horvat to seal the win with his ensuing goal. --Field Level Media

item.title: Karl-Anthony Towns, Knicks avert 0-4 start with victory over Pistons
item.description: Karl-Anthony Towns scored 13 of his game-high 27 points during a decisive third-quarter run as the host New York Knicks rallied past the Detroit Pistons 111-97 on Tuesday for their first win of the season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Karl-Anthony Towns scored 13 of his game-high 27 points during a decisive third-quarter run as the host New York Knicks rallied past the Detroit Pistons 111-97 on Tuesday for their first win of the season. New York trailed by 13 points in the first quarter. The Knicks outscored the Pistons 37-13 in the third and held off a fourth-quarter rally to avoid becoming the first defending NBA champion to open 0-4 since the Boston Celtics in 1969-70. Towns also pulled down a season-high 20 rebounds. Jalen Brunson produced 23 points and seven assists for New York while OG Anunoby and reserve Landry Shamet scored 13 points apiece. Mikal Bridges finished with 12 points, and Andre Drummond added 10 points off the bench. The result snapped the Knicks' six-game losing streak against the Pistons, who won all three games between the teams last season by an average margin of 28 points. Paul Reed had 22 points and nine rebounds for the Pistons, who were seeking their first 4-0 start since the 2018-19 season. Cade Cunningham (19 points, nine rebounds, eight assists) flirted with a triple-double while Duncan Robinson recorded 12 points. Detroit's Ausar Thompson and reserve Daniss Jenkins each had 11 points. The Pistons ended the first quarter on a 15-5 run and took a 38-25 lead on Reed's 3-pointer with 2.8 seconds left. Drummond and Shamet sparked the Knicks' comeback bid in the second. They scored the first 11 points in a half-ending 19-8 run. Brunson sank two free throws with 2.4 seconds remaining to give New York the lead for good at 51-50. The Knicks remained hot to open the third quarter, when they scored the first 11 points to take a double-digit lead. Shamet's 3-pointer with 2:59 left in the period gave New York its first 20-plus-point lead at 82-61. The Knicks were up 88-63 when Josh Hart ended the third with a 3-pointer, and they extended the gap to 27 when Towns began the fourth with a layup. The Pistons outscored New York 34-21 the rest of the way and got as close as 104-93 on Ronald Holland II's putback dunk with 2:39 remaining. --Field Level Media

item.title: Early power-play goals power Panthers over struggling Jets
item.description: Carter Verhaeghe scored two power-play goals and Matthew Tkachuk had four assists to lead the visiting Florida Panthers to a 5-1 win over the Winnipeg Jets on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Carter Verhaeghe scored two power-play goals and Matthew Tkachuk had four assists to lead the visiting Florida Panthers to a 5-1 win over the Winnipeg Jets on Tuesday night. Brady Tkachuk contributed a goal and two assists, Niko Mikkola had a goal and an assist and Sam Reinhart also scored for the Panthers, who went 3-for-5 with the man advantage and won their second straight. Defenseman Seth Jones collected three assists and Akira Schmid made 24 saves. Adam Lowry got the goal for the Jets, who lost their sixth in a row (0-4-2). Clay Stevenson stopped 19 shots. Florida took a 3-0 lead in the first period. The Panthers scored twice in 1:15 to go up 2-0, connecting on two of their first four shots. Verhaeghe produced his first power-play goal at 7:27 to open the scoring. He stepped from below the goal line to the left of the net and put in a backhand shot. And at 8:42, Mikkola's shot from the left circle went in off the stick of Winnipeg defenseman Mario Ferraro. Verhaeghe got his second power-play goal with 9:42 left in the first on a one-timer from the high slot. Lowry's short-handed goal with 7:33 left in the second period made it 3-1. After a giveaway to Lowry by Schmid at the left side of the net, Lowry quickly went behind the net for a wraparound and barely got the puck over the goal line past the stick of the diving Schmid. The play continued for a few seconds, as if Schmid made the save, but the horn blew that signals that league officials watching the game from Toronto ruled the puck went in after immediately reviewing the play. Florida restored the three-goal lead 47 seconds later on Reinhart's power-play goal, a one-time shot from the slot. Brady Tkachuk tipped in a pass from his brother Matthew Tkachuk with 7:50 remaining. The teams play again with the Panthers hosting in Sunshine, Fla., on Friday. It will be the second of back-to-back games for the Jets, who visit the Tampa Bay Lightning on Thursday night. --Field Level Media

item.title: Indian rupee stumbles on oil strain; mild inflows and intervention cap fall
item.description: The Indian rupee was on the defensive on Wednesday, strained by elevated oil prices while modest foreign portfolio inflows and likely intervention by the central bank contained the decline.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Kalra
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee was on the defensive on Wednesday, strained by elevated oil prices while modest foreign portfolio inflows and likely intervention by the central bank contained the decline. The rupee was at 95.19 per dollar as of 11 a.m. IST, down slightly from its close at 95.1150 in the previous session. Oil prices climbed more than 1% after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia renewed concerns around supply risks from the major exporter. Brent oil was last at $115.5 per barrel, hovering near its highest since April. India imports nearly 90% of its crude requirements, making it one of the world's most vulnerable economies to the Middle East oil shock. The vulnerability has kept up pressure on the rupee despite a host of policy measures taken since June to shore up the unit alongside frequent market interventions by the Reserve Bank of India. On Wednesday as well, traders said that state-run banks were spotted offering dollars, most likely on behalf of the RBI. Likely foreign portfolio inflows also aided the rupee in early trading, one of the traders said. This helped the rupee hold up better than its Asian peers, which were down between 0.1% and 1%, with the Korean won leading losses. Indian stocks were faring worse than peers with MSCI's gauge of Asian shares (.MIAP00000PUS) up 1.4% while India's benchmark Nifty 50 (.NSEI) fell 0.7%. Investors are keeping a keen eye on developments in the Middle East while also awaiting the Federal Reserve's policy decision later on Wednesday. Market participants and economists widely expect the US central bank to keep policy rates unchanged. "With little policy surprise anticipated, markets will turn to the guidance ... A hawkish tone would reinforce rate hike expectations, keep US yields elevated, and weigh broadly on Asian FX," MUFG said in a note.

item.title: Netanyahu y Eisenkot se disputan el liderazgo de Israel tras una votación que acabaría en empate
item.description: El primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu y su rival Gadi Eisenkot ofrecieron razones contrapuestas para liderar Israel tras las elecciones del martes: Netanyahu abogó por un gobierno de derechas, mientras que Eisenkot dijo que los votantes habían rechazado al veterano líder israelí, a pesar de que los sondeos a pie de urna apuntaban a un empate entre sus bloques.
item.dc:creator: Maayan Lubell, Lili Bayer, Tamar Beeri
item.content:encoded: El primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu y su rival Gadi Eisenkot ofrecieron razones contrapuestas para liderar Israel tras las elecciones del martes: Netanyahu abogó por un gobierno de derechas, mientras que Eisenkot dijo que los votantes habían rechazado al veterano líder israelí, a pesar de que los sondeos a pie de urna apuntaban a un empate entre sus bloques. Netanyahu abogó por la formación de "un gobierno nacional fuerte y de derechas", mientras que Eisenkot dijo que la ciudadanía había votado en contra de que Netanyahu siguiera como primer ministro y le instó a retirarse de la política. Ninguno de los dos se atribuyó la victoria. Ninguna de las dos declaraciones resolvió el rompecabezas electoral. A medida que iban llegando los resultados definitivos, los sondeos a pie de urna de Kan 11 y el Canal 13 situaban a los bloques empatados a 51-51, mientras que el Canal 12 otorgaba al bloque liderado por el Likud de Netanyahu una estrecha ventaja de 52-49. Ninguna de ellas otorgaba a ninguna de las partes los 61 escaños necesarios para obtener la mayoría en la Knesset, que cuenta con 120 escaños. Este punto muerto podría favorecer a Netanyahu, lo que le permitiría permanecer en el cargo como primer ministro en funciones durante lo que probablemente serán unas prolongadas negociaciones de coalición o incluso hasta que se puedan celebrar nuevas elecciones. Se preveía que los partidos religiosos de extrema derecha liderados por Itamar Ben-Gvir y Bezalel Smotrich obtuvieran un total de 13 escaños dentro del bloque de Netanyahu, sin avances significativos para ninguno de ellos. Los partidos árabes ajenos a los dos bloques principales podrían tener la balanza del poder en sus manos. Sin embargo, Eisenkot, líder del partido Yashar y antiguo jefe del Ejército, ha descartado prácticamente formar un gobierno con ellos, lo que complica su camino hacia el poder. SE INTENSIFICA LA LUCHA POR LA SEGURIDAD Netanyahu destacó los éxitos militares de Israel y planteó la posibilidad de una nueva acción conjunta con el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, contra Irán, en su discurso ante los adherentes del partido, pronunciado pasada la 3 de la madrugada (0100 GMT) en la sede electoral del Likud en Jerusalén. "Israel se enfrenta a una oportunidad histórica única, junto con nuestro socio, el presidente Trump, para eliminar de una vez por todas la amenaza existencial que supone Irán. Pero los motivos ocultos no deben desviarnos de esta misión sagrada", afirmó. Eisenkot había advertido anteriormente a Netanyahu de que no utilizara la seguridad de Israel con fines políticos. "Netanyahu es un primer ministro en funciones, sin mandato ni la confianza del pueblo", señaló Eisenkot, instando a las fuerzas de seguridad a "mantenerse firmes" frente a cualquier intento de anteponer los intereses políticos a la seguridad de Israel. La participación electoral fue del 77,7%, según la Comisión Electoral Central de Israel, la más alta en más de dos décadas y unos 7 puntos porcentuales superior a la de 2022. Se espera que los resultados definitivos se den a conocer el jueves o el viernes, y el fragmentado sistema político israelí da un poder decisivo a los partidos más pequeños en las negociaciones de coalición, que en elecciones anteriores se han prolongado durante semanas o meses. Si ninguno de los bloques logra formar gobierno, podría ser necesario celebrar nuevas elecciones, algo a lo que Eisenkot se opuso dada la elevada participación electoral. Yohanan Plesner, presidente del Instituto para la Democracia de Israel, calificó las encuestas a pie de urna como una gran derrota para la coalición de Netanyahu, pero advirtió de que Eisenkot no se había erigido en claro ganador y que la situación podría cambiar considerablemente a medida que se fueran contando los votos. REVÉS PARA NETANYAHU, SIN GANADOR CLARO Si se confirman las proyecciones de los sondeos a pie de urna, la coalición nacionalista-religiosa de Netanyahu, que en su momento álgido llegó a contar con 68 escaños, se quedaría muy por debajo de los 61 necesarios para gobernar, lo que le dejaría sin un camino claro para formar gobierno. Eisenkot, de 66 años, que perdió a un hijo y a dos sobrinos en la guerra de Gaza, se ha erigido como el rival más fuerte de Netanyahu, haciendo hincapié en su trayectoria en materia de seguridad al tiempo que se posiciona como centrista en el ámbito nacional. Entró en política hace solo cuatro años y se unió al gabinete de guerra de Netanyahu tras el ataque de Hamás de 2023, pero dimitió ocho meses después, criticando el liderazgo del primer ministro. Eisenkot propone romper con el liderazgo de Netanyahu y sus aliados de extrema derecha, pero no con el enfoque de línea dura en materia de seguridad que se ha afianzado aún más desde el ataque de Hamás de 2023. Se opone a la creación de un Estado palestino y dice que el ala militar de Hamás debe ser destruida o desmantelada. Eisenkot dice que la respuesta de Israel —una guerra que ha causado la muerte de más de 74.000 palestinos, según las autoridades sanitarias de Gaza— fue un fracaso porque Hamás sigue al mando. En la sede de la Lista Conjunta, una alianza de varios partidos árabes, se escucharon silbidos y aplausos cuando se publicaron las encuestas a pie de urna, en una noche histórica por la participación de los ciudadanos palestinos de Israel. "Rechazamos la ocupación y el racismo, y nos quedaremos aquí", afirmó Faten Gattas, candidata de la Lista Conjunta, en un discurso pronunciado en la sede de la alianza en Nazaret. Los candidatos esperaban que la elevada participación árabe les permitiera desempeñar un papel decisivo a la hora de impedir que la coalición de Netanyahu vuelva al poder. UN VEREDICTO EN TIEMPOS DE GUERRA Los votantes se enfrentaban al trauma del día más sangriento de Israel, cuando Hamás mató a 1.200 personas y tomó 251 rehenes, así como a las guerras en Gaza y contra Hezbolá del Líbano e Irán que le siguieron. Aunque Netanyahu fue criticado por el mayor fracaso de seguridad del país, argumentó que había hecho que Israel y el mundo fueran más seguros al eliminar a los principales líderes de Hamás, Hezbolá e Irán. Las políticas de la coalición de derecha de Netanyahu han sido motivo de división a nivel nacional y han agravado el aislamiento internacional de Israel, pero él se ha presentado como el líder con la entereza necesaria para plantar cara a los enemigos de Israel. Netanyahu, de 77 años, ha ocupado el cargo de primer ministro durante casi 19 de los últimos 30 años y ha sobrevivido en repetidas ocasiones a crisis políticas. Sus oponentes solo han logrado arrebatarle la presidencia del Gobierno una vez desde 2009, tras cuatro elecciones sin resultado claro en dos años. Dieciocho meses después, volvió al poder. Se presentó a las elecciones enfrentándose a acusaciones de corrupción de larga data, que él niega, y a críticas por los fallos de los servicios de inteligencia que permitieron a los militantes liderados por Hamás llevar a cabo su ataque.

item.title: Canes edge Bruins in clash of Eastern Conference division leaders
item.description: Sebastian Aho scored the tiebreaking goal in the third period, and goalie Pyotr Kochetkov extended his hot start as the Carolina Hurricanes beat the Boston Bruins 2-1 on Tuesday night at Raleigh, N.C.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Sebastian Aho scored the tiebreaking goal in the third period, and goalie Pyotr Kochetkov extended his hot start as the Carolina Hurricanes beat the Boston Bruins 2-1 on Tuesday night at Raleigh, N.C. In a matchup of Eastern Conference division leaders, Jackson Blake also scored for the Hurricanes, who returned from a 3-1-1 road trip to play their first home game in two weeks. Kochetkov made 14 saves to improve to 8-0-0, tying the best start to a season in franchise history. He matched the mark set five years ago by former teammate Frederik Andersen. Pavel Zacha opened the scoring with a first-period power-play goal for Boston, which had won its previous two games and seven of its last eight. Jeremy Swayman stopped 28 shots. A wild sequence preceded Aho's goal. Boston's Matthew Poitras had an open backhand shot bounce off the post before the Bruins retained possession. The Hurricanes eventually freed the puck and transitioned to offense, with Aho poking it into the net from the crease with 9:41 remaining for his eighth goal. Carolina killed off two power plays in the final five minutes. Zacha scored 1:31 into the game, taking advantage of crisp puck movement to easily knock in Elias Lindholm's pass on the power play. Carolina threatened to halt some of Boston's momentum a few minutes later, but Swayman thwarted Nikolaj Ehlers on a breakaway. Blake scored with 52 seconds left in the opening period, converting in front of the net amid three Boston defenders. His point streak reached four games, with two goals and four assists during that span. Neither team scored in the second period, though Carolina held an 8-2 edge in shots on goal. The Hurricanes ended the period with 12 seconds remaining on a 5-on-3 advantage, but they were unable to convert on the power play to start the third. Carolina, the defending Stanley Cup champion, entered the game with 20 points. It was the first team in the NHL to reach that mark this season, a first in franchise history. --Field Level Media

item.title: Blackhawks take down Kings to end 3-game skid
item.description: Wyatt Kaiser and Roman Kantserov scored and Spencer Knight made 25 saves as the host Chicago Blackhawks defeated the Los Angeles Kings 2-1 on Tuesday to stop a three-game losing streak.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Wyatt Kaiser and Roman Kantserov scored and Spencer Knight made 25 saves as the host Chicago Blackhawks defeated the Los Angeles Kings 2-1 on Tuesday to stop a three-game losing streak. Chicago capped a 3-4 homestand while Los Angeles ended a five-game road trip at 3-2. The Blackhawks managed two goals or fewer five times during the stretch, but Kaiser helped the club to a victory with his first goal of the season at 7:17 of the third period. A Kings turnover in the defensive zone created an opportunity for the Blackhawks, with Kaiser sending a wrist shot from the left circle through the five-hole of Los Angeles goaltender Anton Forsberg. Forsberg made 25 saves for the Kings, who tallied a season-best six goals in Monday's victory against the New York Rangers. Quinton Byfield paced the Kings with six shots. Alex Laferriere followed with five. Los Angeles took a 1-0 lead 2:31 into the first period, emerging with a goal after the Blackhawks were unable to clear a puck sitting on the red line. Samuel Helenius stuffed a shot past Knight for his first goal of the season. After registering just one shot over the first five-plus minutes of the game, the Blackhawks ramped up their attack. Forsberg turned aside Patrick Kane's slick backhand move midway through the first period and denied Artyom Levshunov on an odd-man rush in the opening moments of the second. Kantserov tied the game at 1 with a power-play goal at 16:40 of the second period, putting a bouncing puck past Forsberg off a feed from Connor Bedard. Chicago capitalized on the second of consecutive penalties against the Kings' Joel Armia. Referees whistled the Blackhawks' Sam Rinzel for a four-minute double-minor for high-sticking late in the period but Chicago killed the penalty, which overlapped into the third. The Blackhawks went 1-for-3 on the man advantage while the Kings were 0-for-3. --Field Level Media

item.title: US military says it struck vessel in Eastern Pacific, killing five
item.description: The US military said on Tuesday five people were killed in a strike on a vessel in the Eastern Pacific, the latest in a series of attacks that Washington says targets "narco-terrorists" but human rights experts condemn as extrajudicial killings.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: The US military said on Tuesday five people were killed in a strike on a vessel in the Eastern Pacific, the [USN:L1N452014 TEXT:"latest in a series of attacks"] that Washington says targets "narco-terrorists" but human rights experts condemn as extrajudicial killings. The US Southern Command "executed a lethal, kinetic strike on a go-fast vessel operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Eastern Pacific," it said on X It cited what it called "confirmed intelligence" to allege the vessel was actively involved in drug trafficking, without providing more details It said five people were killed, describing them as "narco-terrorists" President Donald Trump's administration has said the vessels it has struck since September 2025 were transporting narcotics US strikes on such vessels in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific have killed more than 230 people Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International and independent [USN:L1N3W20V1 TEXT:"UN experts"] have called the strikes unlawful extrajudicial killings while the American Civil Liberties Union has cast assertions by Trump's administration against those it targets as "unsubstantiated, fear-mongering claims" (This story has been refiled to change 'ships' to 'vessels' in paragraph 6.)

item.title: Connor Hellebuyck wins Devils debut, making 17 saves to beat Stars
item.description: The Connor Hellebuyck era began with a win for the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday, as the recently acquired star goaltender stopped 17 shots in a 5-1 victory over the host Dallas Stars.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Connor Hellebuyck era began with a win for the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday, as the recently acquired star goaltender stopped 17 shots in a 5-1 victory over the host Dallas Stars. New Jersey extended its winning streak to four games while snapping Dallas' five-game winning run. Given his first start four days after being acquired from the Winnipeg Jets in a blockbuster trade, the three-time Vezina Trophy winner made his season debut after last playing on April 13. Captain Nico Hischier scored twice for New Jersey, while Luke Hughes and Jack Hughes each had a goal and an assist. Jesper Boqvist also tallied. Justin Hryckowian produced Dallas' lone goal, and Casey DeSmith stopped 22 of 27 shots. Hischier opened the scoring early 2:41 into the first period, holding onto the puck before sliding a shot past a sprawling DeSmith. Jack Hughes was forced to leave the game briefly midway through the opening period after taking a high-stick to the face and appearing to spit out a tooth. He returned later with a full face shield. Just 38 seconds into the second period, Hischier added a second goal with a snap shot, beating DeSmith low on his glove side to double the lead. Just past the game's midpoint, Boqvist extended the lead to 3-0. Dallas' Jamie Benn and New Jersey's Brenden Dillon dropped the gloves as play resumed after Boqvist's goal, before Hryckowian cut the deficit to two by deflecting Tyler Myers' wrist shot from the point at 16:08 in the second to beat Hellebuyck. Luke Hughes restored the visitors' lead just 28 seconds later. Early in the final frame, Stars blue-liner Kyle Capobianco limped off with an apparent lower-body injury after a hit from Timo Meier. Jack Hughes netted an additional insurance goal to extend the lead to 5-1 at 13:15 into the third. The Devils were opening a three-game road trip that continues Wednesday at Colorado. The Stars fell to 3-1-0 on a six-game homestand. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jayson Tatum's buzzer-beating jumper lifts Celtics over Nets in OT
item.description: Jayson Tatum made an elbow jumper as time expired in overtime to give the Boston Celtics a 125-124 victory over the visiting Brooklyn Nets on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jayson Tatum made an elbow jumper as time expired in overtime to give the Boston Celtics a 125-124 victory over the visiting Brooklyn Nets on Tuesday night. Tatum scored a game-high 40 points and made a career-high 18 free throws on 22 attempts. Paul George added 20 points, seven rebounds and seven assists for Boston. Michael Porter Jr. led the Nets with 27 points and 12 rebounds. Julius Randle finished with 24 points and nine rebounds. Brooklyn trailed 117-114 late in the fourth, but Mikel Brown Jr. sent the game to overtime by making a 3-pointer with one second left in regulation. Boston trailed 124-123 in overtime when it took possession with 2.3 seconds to play, enough time for Tatum to sink the game-winning shot. The Celtics led 24-21 late in the first quarter, but a 10-0 run put Brooklyn up by seven. The Nets led 31-26 after one quarter. An 8-0 run by the Celtics tied the game, 45-45, but Brooklyn had a 61-56 halftime lead. Boston was 2 of 16 on 3-point attempts in the half. The Celtics were within one, 71-70, following a Jordan Walsh 3-pointer with 7:40 remaining in the third, but the Nets regained the momentum by scoring the next six points. Boston shaved Brooklyn's lead to 79-78 following a Baylor Scheierman 3-pointer with 2:20 remaining in the third, and took an 81-79 lead on a Tatum 3-pointer with 1:18 left in the quarter. Boston made eight 3-pointers in the third quarter and had an 86-82 lead entering the fourth. The Celtics had their largest lead, 90-82, after they scored the first four points in the final quarter, but the Nets regained the lead on a Brown 3-pointer that capped a 9-0 run and made it 99-97 with 6:42 left. Brooklyn had a 109-104 advantage, but Tatum tied the game on a layup and Boston went in front 111-109 on two Derrick White free throws with 1:40 to play. --Field Level Media

item.title: Grand jury declines to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson, source says
item.description: A federal grand jury has declined to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson who had provided testimony to a congressional panel that probed the January 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol by President Donald Trump's supporters, a source familiar with the matter said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Goudsward, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: A federal grand jury has declined to indict former White House aide [USN:L1N33C1OW TEXT:"Cassidy Hutchinson"] who had provided testimony to a congressional panel that probed the January 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol by President Donald Trump's supporters, a source familiar with the matter said on Tuesday. The Justice Department of the Trump administration has been investigating Hutchinson over whether she gave false testimony to the congressional panel. Hutchinson has maintained that her testimony was truthful. A second source said the grand jury weighing evidence in the case had been meeting Tuesday but did not know if the indictment had been rejected. A federal prosecutor told US Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui during a court hearing that a grand jury in Washington had rejected an indictment but the prosecutor did not reveal in court the proposed defendant or charges. Political experts have raised concerns about efforts by the Trump administration to target his critics and political opponents. After weeks of Trump's false claims that he had won the 2020 elections, his supporters had stormed the US Capitol on January 6, 2021, in an unsuccessful attempt to prevent the congressional certification of those elections. Trump [USN:S0N3O6042 TEXT:"pardoned nearly everyone"] criminally charged with participating in the 2021 Capitol attack on his first day back in office for a second term in January 2025. Former Justice Department special counsel Jack Smith and his team secured an indictment in 2023, accusing Trump of plotting to overturn his defeat in the 2020 election. Smith dropped that and another case after Trump won the 2024 election, citing a Justice Department policy against prosecuting a sitting president.

item.title: Danish Brewer Carlsberg files updated papers for India unit's IPO
item.description: Danish brewer Carlsberg's India unit moved closer to a public listing as it filed an updated draft prospectus for an initial public offering late on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Danish brewer Carlsberg's (CARLb.CO) India unit moved closer to a public listing as it filed an updated draft prospectus for an initial public offering late on Tuesday. This is the first public IPO prospectus from Carlsberg India, which had confidentially filed papers for the planned offering in July. India's markets regulator [USN:L6N45N0SO TEXT:"approved"] it earlier this month. The IPO is entirely an offer for sale of 86.42 million shares, the draft prospectus dated October 27 showed. The move adds to a string of multinational companies turning to Indian equity markets to monetise their investments, rather than raise fresh capital. Hyundai Motor (005380.KS) and [USN:L3N3VV09T TEXT:"LG Electronics"] (066570.KS) have both pursued stake sales via Indian IPOs, attracted by relatively richer market valuations. The potential listing would add to a busy period for India's IPO market, where large offerings from [USN:L3N46D1BO TEXT:"Jio Platforms"] (JIOP.NS) and [USN:L4N45G0A8 TEXT:"National Stock Exchange of India"] (NSEI.BO) have shown strong investor appetite. Carlsberg India operates through seven breweries it owns and nine third party manufacturers in India. It has a market share of 21.9% in 16 key states and union territories in Asia's third-largest economy, the updated prospectus showed. The Indian unit's profit for the quarter ended June dropped 3.9% to 1.58 billion rupees ($16.61 million), while net revenue rose 21.5% to 13.66 billion rupees, as per the updated draft prospectus. Carlsberg India's listed peers include United Breweries (UBBW.NS) , United Spirits (UNSP.NS) , Radico Khaitan (RADC.NS) , and Allied Blenders and Distillers (ALLE.NS) . ($1 = 95.12 Indian rupees)

item.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot stake rival claims to lead Israel after deadlocked vote
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for a right-wing government and rival Gadi Eisenkot said voters had rejected the longtime Israeli leader, even as exit polls left their blocs deadlocked.
item.dc:creator: Maayan Lubell, Lili Bayer, Tamar Beeri
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot offered competing claims to lead Israel after Tuesday's election, with Netanyahu calling for a right-wing government and Eisenkot saying voters had rejected the longtime Israeli leader, even as exit polls left their blocs deadlocked. While the projected results would represent a setback for Netanyahu and his nationalist-religious coalition, the deadlock could work in his favour, leaving the 77-year-old in office as a caretaker prime minister during what are likely to be prolonged coalition negotiations or even until another election can be held. With vote counts trickling in, Kan 11 and Channel 13 exit polls had the blocs tied at 51 seats each, while Channel 12 gave Netanyahu's Likud-led bloc a narrow 52-49 edge. That left both sides short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, and neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot claimed victory. Tuesday's vote was the first election since the Hamas-led attack of October 7, 2023, and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. Far-right religious parties led by Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich were projected to take a combined 13 seats within Netanyahu's bloc – with no major gains for either of them. Arab parties outside the two main blocs could hold the balance of power. But Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party and a former military chief, has all but ruled out forming a government with them, complicating his path to power. SECURITY FIGHT SHARPENS Netanyah, addressing party faithful after 3 a.m. (0100 GMT) at Likud election headquarters in Jerusalem, called for the formation of “a strong, right-wing national government.” He also highlighted Israel's military successes and raised the prospect of renewed joint action with US President Donald Trump against Iran. "Israel faces a singular historical opportunity, together with our partner President Trump, to remove the existential threat of Iran once and for all. But ulterior motives must not divert us from this sacred mission," he said. Eisenkot said the public had voted against Netanyahu remaining prime minister and called on him to retire from politics, while warning him not to use Israel's security for political purposes. “Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister, without a mandate or the people's trust,” Eisenkot said, calling on the security establishment to “stand firm” against any attempt to put political interests ahead of Israel's security. Voter turnout was 77.7%, Israel's Central Elections Committee said, the highest in more than two decades and around 7 percentage points higher than in 2022. Final results are expected on Thursday or Friday, and Israel's fragmented political system leaves smaller parties potential kingmakers in coalition negotiations that have run to weeks or months after past elections. If neither bloc can form a government, another vote may need to be held, something Eisenkot opposed given the high voter turnout. Yohanan Plesner, president of the Israel Democracy Institute, called the exit polls a major defeat for Netanyahu's coalition but cautioned that Eisenkot had not emerged as a clear winner and much could change as votes were counted. The Israeli shekel weakened modestly on the indecisive result. NETANYAHU SETBACK, NO CLEAR WINNER If the exit poll projections hold, Netanyahu's right-wing bloc, which at its height held 68 seats, would fall far short of the 61 needed to govern, leaving him with no clear path to forming a government. Eisenkot, 66, who lost a son and two nephews in the Gaza war, emerged as Netanyahu's strongest challenger, stressing his security credentials while positioning himself as a centrist domestically. He entered politics only four years ago and joined Netanyahu's war cabinet after the 2023 Hamas attack, but quit eight months later, criticising the prime minister's leadership. [USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"Eisenkot offers a break"] with Netanyahu's leadership and far-right allies, but not with the hawkish approach to security that has become more entrenched since the 2023 Hamas attack. He opposes Palestinian statehood and says Hamas' military wing must be destroyed or dismantled. Eisenkot says Israel's response — a war that has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians, according to Gaza health authorities — was a failure because Hamas remains in charge. The headquarters of the Joint List, an alliance of several Arab parties, burst into whistles and applause when exit polls were released, on a historic night for turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel. “We refuse the occupation and racism, and we will remain here,” said Faten Gattas, a candidate in the Joint List, in a speech at the alliance’s headquarters in Nazareth. Candidates hoped high Arab turnout would allow them to play a decisive role in blocking Netanyahu's coalition from returning to power. A WARTIME VERDICT Voters grappled with the trauma of Israel's deadliest day, when Hamas killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostage, and the wars in Gaza and with Lebanon's Hezbollah and Iran that followed. While Netanyahu was criticised for the country's biggest security failure, he argued that he had made Israel and the world safer by killing top leaders of Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran. The policies of Netanyahu's right-wing coalition have been divisive at home and deepened Israel's international isolation, but he has portrayed himself as the leader with the mettle to face down Israel's foes. Netanyahu, 77, has served as prime minister for nearly 19 of the past 30 years and has repeatedly survived political crises. His opponents have managed to wrest the premiership from him only once since 2009, after four inconclusive elections in two years. Eighteen months later, he was back. He entered the election facing long-standing corruption charges, which he denies, and criticism over intelligence failures that allowed Hamas-led militants to carry out their attack.

item.title: Spurs nearly flawless in 80-point first half, keep Kings winless
item.description: Victor Wembanyama poured in 29 points and grabbed 10 rebounds in just 27 minutes, and Julian Champagnie canned eight first-half 3-pointers as the host San Antonio Spurs steamrolled the Sacramento Kings 130-103 on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Victor Wembanyama poured in 29 points and grabbed 10 rebounds in just 27 minutes, and Julian Champagnie canned eight first-half 3-pointers as the host San Antonio Spurs steamrolled the Sacramento Kings 130-103 on Tuesday. The Spurs led by 10 at the end of the opening period and by 26 at halftime after a combined 47 points from Wembanyama and Champagnie in the first two quarters. San Antonio set league season highs for points (80), assists (23) and 3-pointers (13) in a half in a near-complete performance before the break. Sacramento never got closer than 23 points in the third quarter as the Spurs carried a 107-80 lead into the final period. The visitors never challenged San Antonio's lead in the fourth, but Sacramento's reserves made the final score a little more respectable. Champagnie, who played 25 minutes off the bench, finished with 26 points.
