Stephon Castle added 15, Devin Vassell and Keldon Johnson scored 14 apiece, Dylan Harper had 13 and De'Aaron Fox tallied 11 for the Spurs, who won their second straight game in the first half of a home-road back-to-back that continues Wednesday in Utah. De'Andre Hunter led the Kings with 24 points, Zach LaVine added 22, Darius Acuff Jr. scored 19 and Domantas Sabonis amassed 20 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists. Sacramento has opened the season with four straight losses and has surrendered at least 121 points in each game. The Spurs got 15 points from Wembanyama and three 3-pointers from Vassell in the first quarter, building a 12-point lead before settling for a 39-29 advantage. The second quarter was more of the same as Champagnie kept shooting -- and making -- shots from distance. His eighth 3-pointer, and sixth of the period, pushed the Spurs' lead to 68-43 at the 4:23 mark. Wembanyama crashed the glass for a final tip-in at the buzzer to give San Antonio its biggest lead of the half, 80-54, as the teams went to halftime. Champagnie led all scorers with 24 points at the break, while Wembanyama had 23 as the Spurs shot 60% from the floor and 59.1% from beyond the arc. Sabonis paced the Kings with 16 points, while Acuff had 13. --Field Level Media

item.title: Indian shares fall as oil rise weighs; Jio lists at 21.4% premium
item.description: Indian shares fell on Wednesday as rising oil prices weighed on risk appetite ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy decision later in the day.
item.dc:creator: Bharath Rajeswaran
item.content:encoded: Indian shares fell on Wednesday as rising oil prices weighed on risk appetite ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy decision later in the day. Meanwhile, Jio Platforms (JIOP.NS) listed at a 21.4% premium over its issue price, making it the second-largest publicly traded firm in the country by market value. The benchmark Nifty 50 (.NSEI) fell 0.41% to 22,657.35, and the Sensex (.BSESN) shed 0.61% to 73,153.6, as of 9:55 a.m.(0425 GMT). In contrast, the broader small-caps (.NIFSMCP100) and mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100) gained 0.7% and 0.1%, outperforming benchmarks for the third straight session after they dropped 7.3% and 5.6% last week. Eleven of the 16 major sectors logged losses. IT stocks (.NIFTYIT) , which earn a significant share of their revenue from the US, dropped 3.1%, leading the sectoral losses. Infosys (INFY.NS) fell 4.4% while TCS (TCS.NS) and HCLTech (HCLT.NS) dropped 3% each. O il prices climbed 1.4% to $115.4 a barrel after an [USN:L6N46D0XG TEXT:"attack"] on a refinery in top exporter Saudi Arabia renewed concerns about energy supply disruptions and inflation. However, a post-results rally in Bajaj Auto (BAJA.NS) and Larsen & Toubro (LART.NS) , which rose 3% and 4.2%, respectively, limited some of the benchmarks' losses. "For the Indian market to revive, crude prices have to decline and FPIs have to stop their relentless selling and turn buyers," said VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments. "For this to happen, changes in the long-term capital gains tax appear inevitable now. There is a high probability of this happening since the massive FPI outflows have started hurting India's otherwise good macros." Among stocks, Max Financial (MAXI.NS) fell 2.2% after reporting its quarterly earnings. Quarterly growth slowed significantly across key channels, said analysts at JPMorgan, adding that the stock is likely to be under pressure after the results, given slowing growth and overhang of distribution reforms. Bucking the trend, Raymond (RYMD.NS) jumped 3.5% after posting a roughly 97% year-on-year rise in second-quarter profit. Subros (SUBR.NS) gained 2.6% after securing a contract worth 12.25 billion rupees ($128.79 million) from Maruti Suzuki (MRTI.NS) . ($1 = 95.1150 Indian rupees)

item.title: Wawrinka brings career to a close with defeat in Basel
item.description: Three-time Grand Slam champion Stan Wawrinka played the final match of his career in front of home fans on Tuesday, bidding farewell to the sport following a 7-5 7-6(2) defeat by Czech Jiri Lehecka at the Swiss Indoors in Basel.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Three-time Grand Slam champion Stan Wawrinka played the final match of his career in front of home fans on Tuesday, bidding farewell to the sport following a 7-5 7-6(2) defeat by Czech Jiri Lehecka at the Swiss Indoors in Basel. Wawrinka announced last year that he would retire at the end of the 2026 season, 24 years after he turned professional. The 41-year-old defeated Rafa Nadal in the 2014 Australian Open final to win his first major, before claiming his other two Grand Slam crowns by beating Novak Djokovic in the finals of the 2015 French Open and 2016 US Open. "For me, all I wanted in my career was to give everything, to have no regrets, to always fight, to always give 100% in every match — out of respect for myself, for the opponent, for the tournament, for the fans, for everybody," Wawrinka told the ATP website. "That was always the most important thing for more than 20 years, and that's the only way you can leave the sport: without any regrets." Wawrinka won 16 ATP titles and reached a career-high world ranking of number three in 2014. He also won Olympic doubles gold with Roger Federer in 2008 and helped deliver Switzerland's first Davis Cup title in 2014.

item.title: China's Dongshan Precision shares fall 2.1% in Hong Kong debut
item.description: Chinese printed circuit board maker Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing dropped 2.1% in its Hong Kong trading debut on Wednesday, after raising HK$9.88 billion ($1.26 billion) in its share sale.
item.dc:creator: Yantoultra Ngui
item.content:encoded: Chinese printed circuit board maker Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing dropped 2.1% in its Hong Kong trading debut on Wednesday, after raising HK$9.88 billion ($1.26 billion) in its share sale. The stock opened at HK$82.40 compared with its HK$86.80 offer price, before climbing to HK$85, or about 2.1% lower. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index (.HSI) was up 0.25%, while the Hang Seng Tech Index (.HSTECH) was up 1.22%. "The new listing environment has been quite mediocre lately ... So a weak debut for Dongshan would not surprise me," said Dickie Wong, executive director of research at uSMART Securities. "While interest in names like Anthropic remains strong in the US, the AI supply-chain theme here has already passed its most enthusiastic phase and investors have become more selective," Wong said. Dongshan's debut follows a global tech rout driven by fresh concerns about how long the AI spending boom can last and whether the returns will justify the heavy borrowing in the sector. The firm pushed ahead with the listing after Chinese robot maker Changzhou Microintelligence (3275.HK) and tourism group Jiangsu Slender West Lake Culture and Tourism (6157.HK) [USN:L3N46C0CM TEXT:"delayed"] their planned Hong Kong share sales, citing [USN:FWN4660V7 TEXT:"market conditions"]. Dongshan set its offer price at HK$86.80 per share, about 7.5% below its HK$93.80 maximum price, according to a stock exchange [USN:L3N46B01P TEXT:"filing"] on Sunday. The company did not use its option to increase the deal size, the filing showed. Hong Kong retail investors subscribed for 0.52 times the shares initially set aside for them, while the international offering was 3.17 times subscribed, according to the company's allotment results [USN:FWN46D1XM TEXT:"filing on Tuesday"]. Dongshan moved 5.47 million shares from the Hong Kong retail tranche to the international offering, the filing showed. The deal's cornerstone investors, or large investors that commit to buy shares before a listing, were allocated 56.89 million shares, equal to 50% of the offer, according to the filing. They included Aurora SF, JPMorgan Asset Management (Asia Pacific), Alibaba Investment and CPE Bodhi. The cornerstone shares cannot be sold for six months, the filing showed. Dongshan makes printed circuit boards, automotive parts, display modules and optical transceivers, which send data through fibre-optic cables, according to its listing prospectus. Dongshan plans to use most of the listing proceeds to expand production of high-speed optical chips, optical modules and high-end circuit boards, the prospectus showed.

item.title: Iowa RB Kamari Moulton done for season due to upper-body injury
item.description: Iowa running back Kamari Moulton will miss the rest of the season with an upper-body injury, coach Kirk Ferentz said Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iowa running back Kamari Moulton will miss the rest of the season with an upper-body injury, coach Kirk Ferentz said Tuesday. Moulton left the Hawkeyes' 13-10 loss at Minnesota on Saturday in the second quarter and didn't return. According to reports, Moulton had his right shoulder examined before being moved into the medical tent and was later seen with the arm in a sling following the contest. "Unfortunately, he's going to be done," Ferentz said during his weekly press conference. "We'll look forward to getting him back here, but he's got some rehab to go through." Moulton ranks second in the Big Ten in rushing yards per game at 90.2. By yardage, he stands eighth with 541 in six games. He has rushed for four touchdowns. Moulton twice achieved career highs for rushing yardage this season. He ran for 183 on 11 carries in a season-opening 40-0 rout of Northern Illinois and later had 208 yards on 26 carries in a 41-24 road victory over Washington on Oct. 9. "Kamari is playing his best football this year because of the experience, confidence that you only get by playing," Ferentz said of the senior. "You have to go out and get beat up sometimes to grow true confidence." Xavier Williams is the likely starter for the Hawkeyes (5-2, 2-2 Big Ten) on Saturday against No. 25 Wisconsin. He has rushed for 187 yards and three touchdowns on just 25 carries. L.J. Phillips Jr., who opened the season as the backup running back, is ailing, according to Ferentz. He has rushed for 88 yards on 25 carries. "He got to work a little bit (Tuesday), and (he) will probably be day-to-day, so we'll see what the week brings there," Ferentz said. --Field Level Media

item.title: US closes $5.1 billion loan to Alliant Energy for new gas power generation, energy storage
item.description: The US Department of Energy said on Wednesday it has closed a $5.1 billion loan package to Alliant Energy to expand power generation and bolster the grid at plants in Iowa and Wisconsin.
item.dc:creator: Timothy Gardner
item.content:encoded: The US Department of Energy said on Wednesday it has closed a $5.1 billion loan package to Alliant Energy (LNT.O) to expand power generation and bolster the grid at plants in Iowa and Wisconsin. The investments from the department's loans office will support new natural gas-fired power plants, energy storage systems, and upgrades to existing generation facilities, it said. The loans will create hundreds of construction-related jobs and deliver more than 2.6 gigawatts of new or upgraded power generation capacity, it said. That's enough power for nearly 1.8 million homes. The loan had originally been proposed by the administration of former President Joe Biden in his last days in office in January 2025 when it was only a conditional loan of $3 billion. The office of Energy Dominance Financing, called the Loan Programs Office under Biden, has hundreds of billions of dollars in financing available, the bulk of which Energy Secretary Chris Wright has said will support nuclear power. More than the name of the office has changed. Its mission during the Biden administration was to provide support to emerging clean energy projects and alternative vehicles that struggled to get bank loans. Now it includes support to projects such as natural gas that have typically been able to get bank loans. Energy storage, which typically includes batteries, was supported in both the initial and the closed loan. "By bringing new, dependable power online, we are strengthening our nation’s energy security and lowering electricity costs for families and businesses across Iowa and Wisconsin," the loan office director, Gregory Beard, said in a release. Any lowering of electricity costs could take many years as the loans take place over decades.

item.title: Nearly 90% of businesses are turning to tokenised money, DBS survey shows
item.description: Global adoption of tokenised money is moving faster than expected among businesses looking to improve liquidity management and access new markets, a top executive from Singapore bank DBS said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Global adoption of tokenised money is moving faster than expected among businesses looking to improve liquidity management and access new markets, a top executive from Singapore bank DBS (DBSM.SI) said. The remarks by Lim Soon Chong, the group head of global transaction services, follow a survey by the lender that showed that 88% of businesses have deployed or are piloting tokenised money use cases. Conducted between June and July, the survey polled 422 global business and finance leaders from organisations with annual revenue exceeding $500 million across 11 markets including the US, UK, Australia, China and Germany Roughly two-thirds of respondents said their businesses had either fully deployed tokenised money at scale or begun using it in selected locations Stablecoins were the most widely adopted tokenised instrument at 63%, followed by tokenised deposits at 53% and tokenised money market funds at 52% "Our interpretation is that there are significant benefits that stablecoins offer," said Lim "Stablecoins, as you know, offer better fungibility across payment intermediaries, not just across banks. They are less cumbersome from a permissioning standpoint," he said The survey found Southeast Asia was the top destination for businesses looking to expand into new markets, followed by Australia and New Zealand, with India ranking third More than half of respondents in both Australia and the UK said they were considering using the Chinese renminbi for trade settlement over the next one to two years The renminbi's recent appreciation is making renminbi settlement more attractive to Chinese exporters, who are increasingly offering better commercial terms for transactions denominated in the currency, DBS said "The Chinese authorities are clearly pushing the internationalisation of the renminbi, so we expect this to go up," Lim said

item.title: Kent Johnson scores 2nd goal in OT to lift Jackets over Flyers
item.description: Kent Johnson scored his second goal of the night 2:22 into overtime to lift the visiting Columbus Blue Jackets to a 4-3 triumph over the Philadelphia Flyers on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kent Johnson scored his second goal of the night 2:22 into overtime to lift the visiting Columbus Blue Jackets to a 4-3 triumph over the Philadelphia Flyers on Tuesday. Johnson scored off a feed from Adam Fantilli on the Blue Jackets' second 2-on-0 breakaway of overtime. Dan Vladar had stopped the first rush featuring Cole Sillinger and Zach Werenski but was helpless following a series of back-and-forth passes between Johnson and Fantilli. Fantilli and Denton Mateychuk scored the other goals for Columbus, which squandered a 3-0 lead before escaping with two points. Cam Talbot made 28 saves. Philadelphia's Jamie Drysdale tied the game with 11 seconds left in regulation, after Noah Cates and Trevor Zegras supplied the Flyers' initial goals. Columbus erupted for three goals in less than three minutes in the first period. Fantilli, who scored the OT winner in the Blue Jackets' most recent game, opened the scoring in this one with his fourth of the season. On a 2-on-2 rush, Johnson found Fantilli, whose shot slipped through Vladar for a 1-0 lead. Less than two minutes later, Johnson was the beneficiary of a turnover by Philadelphia rookie Oliver Bonk. Following the miscue behind the net, Werenski took a one-timer from the point that Johnson deflected home for his fifth of the campaign. The Blue Jackets weren't finished, though, as Mateychuk scored just 50 seconds later when he found space in the high slot and took a shot through traffic that evaded Vladar. The Flyers got on the board near the midpoint of the second period as Porter Martone's shot trickled through Talbot and was poked in by Cates for his first goal of the year. Zegras scored off a rebound with 4:56 left in regulation, drawing the hosts within 3-2. Then in the waning seconds of regulation, Zegras made a nice feed to Tyson Foerster, whose centering pass caromed off Drysdale's skate and into the net. With a goal and an assist, Zegras has three goals and six assists during a five-game points streak. --Field Level Media

item.title: No. 25 BYU, Ohio St. tip off in Salt Lake City aiming to make deeper runs
item.description: Expectations are high for Ohio State and No. 25 BYU when they open their seasons Monday in Salt Lake City.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Expectations are high for Ohio State and No. 25 BYU when they open their seasons Monday in Salt Lake City. The goal for each is to advance further than the opening round of the NCAA Tournament. That finish was particularly disappointing for BYU after coach Kevin Young led the Cougars to 26 wins and a Sweet 16 appearance during his first season in 2024-25. Last season, BYU was 23-12 (9-9 Big 12) and was upset by No. 11 seed Texas. For the Buckeyes (21-13, 12-8 Big Ten last season), it was a quick exit in their first trip to the tournament since 2022 when they fell to No. 9 TCU. Ohio State coach Jake Diebler, starting his third full season after an 8-3 record as interim coach in 2023-24, said simply reaching the NCAA Tournament is not good enough. "From Day 1 I've leaned into the standard of this program," he said. "That's the goal, to get back to those peaks of this program. I'm not afraid of those expectations. I'm not afraid of the standard that is this program. In fact, we're trying to take it to the top and that's the mentality I want our guys to have." BYU has some big shoes to fill after relying heavily on AJ Dybantsa, the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft by the Washington Wizards. He led the nation last season in scoring with 25.5 points per game while making 51.0% of his field-goal attempts. Richie Saunders (18.0 ppg, 5.8 rpg in 25 games before a season-ending knee injury) was also selected in the draft with the No. 32 pick by the Memphis Grizzlies. The Cougars will turn to Robert Wright III, who averaged 18.1 points and 4.6 assists last season. "Rob was one of the best point guards in the country last year, and he's improved a lot," BYU associate head coach Tim Fanning said. "His body has improved a lot and his shooting has improved a lot. He's a guy that's clearly on an upward trend just as an individual in his development, and so having a guy like that back is massive for the team. "I think we did a really good job of surrounding him with shooting so I think we're going to be a really tough team to stop." John Mobley Jr. leads the Buckeyes. He averaged 15.7 points per game in his second season and is expected to be ready for the Cougars despite twisting his ankle late in Ohio State's final exhibition game vs. Butler on Oct. 25. "I feel good. I just stepped on a foot. Little roll. Felt there was no need to go back in. It's better off just resting it," Mobley said, emphasizing it was a "minor" injury. He and Amare Bynum are the returning starters. Bynum averaged 9.7 points and 4.9 rebounds as a freshman last season. Bynum agreed with Diebler's assessment that he needs to be more involved in the offense. "Especially in transition, if I see that open lane, I'm going to go and take it and get a bucket," Bynum said. "I know we still have to work on some things before the BYU game. But we just have to keep playing together and we have to be better on defense with a little bit better communication." --Field Level Media

item.title: Wolves brace for Anthony Edwards' absence, face Yaxel Lendeborg, Warriors
item.description: The Minnesota Timberwolves must prepare for life without Anthony Edwards for the foreseeable future as they get ready to host the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday in Minneapolis.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Minnesota Timberwolves must prepare for life without Anthony Edwards for the foreseeable future as they get ready to host the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday in Minneapolis. According to multiple reports Tuesday, the superstar guard will undergo arthroscopic surgery on his ailing right knee and could miss up to two months. Edwards averaged 33.3 points over Minnesota's first four games. He is coming off a 47-point performance on 19-of-34 shooting in a 127-125 overtime loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday. The Timberwolves have several players who could step up during Edwards' absence. Jaden McDaniels ranks second on the team with 15.0 points per game early in the season, while LaMelo Ball, acquired in the offseason to pair with Edwards in the backcourt, is averaging 14.8 points and a team-high 6.3 assists. Third-year guard Terrence Shannon Jr., who is averaging 13 points per game, has earned praise from coaches and teammates for his contributions off the bench. "No doubt about it, there's been great growth there," Timberwolves coach Chris Finch said recently. "There really has been. His contain, his routes, he's not fouling -- he used to be a high-foul guy. The only missing piece for him right now is rebounding at a little bit better level. And that'd be exactly what this lineup needs." Meanwhile, Warriors coach Steve Kerr remains optimistic about his team despite a slow start that included three consecutive losses to open the season. One reason for Kerr's optimism is the emerging chemistry between Brandin Podziemski and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. The pair showed promise in Golden State's first win of the season Monday against Denver and could have another opportunity to work together against Minnesota. "Brandin really knows how to play," Kerr said. "He knows how to get people the ball. He knows how to deal with closeouts. When you have both of them on the floor, there's just a lot that can happen in order to attack the defense. I thought both guys were terrific (against the Nuggets). Together, they really form a nice combo." Lendeborg is averaging 21.8 points on 45% shooting through his first four NBA games. He is also averaging 9.3 rebounds, 4.8 assists and one steal per game. However, he was listed as questionable on Tuesday's injury report with left foot inflammation and soreness. Kerr believes the sky is the limit for the former Michigan Wolverine. "That's the exciting part is where this can go," Kerr said. "Because there's still probably 10 plays that I could pull up on tape where he made mistakes either defensively or offensively, not recognizing something that he needs to recognize. "Despite all that, he just dominated the game (against Denver) and took over -- at 24 (years old) and in his fourth game. So, pretty impressive. We're going to keep coaching him and keep trying to get him to learn the NBA game and make the most of that enormous potential he's got." Stephen Curry leads the Warriors with 23.7 points per game while shooting 52.6% from the field. Lendeborg and Podziemski, who is averaging 18.0 points, are close behind. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rockets finding ways to limit Kevin Durant's load with Bucks up next
item.description: One result from last season that the Houston Rockets were anxious to adjust was Kevin Durant finishing second in the NBA in minutes played in his 18th season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: One result from last season that the Houston Rockets were anxious to adjust was Kevin Durant finishing second in the NBA in minutes played in his 18th season. In their 120-110 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday, the Rockets displayed their superior depth and their waning dependence on Durant. Houston, which will play the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday, pulled away from the Hawks in the fourth quarter with Durant on the bench. "We had a great lineup out there that had some great momentum," said Durant, who totaled 22 points, nine rebounds and four blocks in only 30 minutes. "Coaches are always looking to get me some extra minutes of rest on the bench. If the unit that's in the game is rolling, I'm all for just sitting over there and supporting them and being ready when my number is called." The Rockets extended a six-point lead entering the final period to 117-95 with 4:44 left to play, all while Durant watched from the sideline. Center Alperen Sengun anchored a group that included guards Fred VanVleet and Reed Sheppard, and forwards Jabari Smith Jr. and Tari Eason, a unit that played so well on both ends of the court that Durant was allowed to rest and cheer. "Obviously, we'd like to get his minutes down," Rockets coach Ime Udoka said. "It's great when we can have the luxury of a group out there doing what they did, a selfless group that doesn't care who's really getting it done as long as we're getting it done." Expectations were low for the Bucks entering this season following the offseason trade of franchise icon Giannis Antetokounmpo. After dropping their first three games by an average of 10 points, the Bucks seemed to confirm that season-long struggles were ahead. But a fourth-quarter rally on Monday gave the Bucks a 110-102 home win over the Indiana Pacers, helping them avoid their first 0-4 start since the 1976-77 season. It also marked the first victory for coach Taylor Jenkins, who is in his first season in Milwaukee after being fired by Memphis with only nine games remaining in the 2024-25 campaign. "Still more to clean up, but just really proud of the group," Jenkins said. "(An) 0-3 (start to the season) settles in, and you're down 11 at halftime. We came out and had the right intensity. "Awesome to get the first win and to share it with a special group. This isn't about me. This is about the organization, this is about the team, about my coaching staff. It's about those players that, despite three tough starts to the season, came out at home and found a way to grind it out." The Bucks might develop an advantage with their center rotation of Myles Turner and Kel'el Ware. Turner posted nine rebounds, four assists and four blocks against his former team while Ware scored 16 points and grabbed 14 rebounds in 19 minutes off the bench. "Those guys did it in different ways," Jenkins said of Turner and Ware. "Just really proud of the growth that they're making, trying to still figure out our defensive system and still making an impact. "They've got more from growth, and I know they're excited about what imprint they can make on the defensive side for us." --Field Level Media

item.title: Oil rises over 1% after Saudi Arabian refinery attack reignites supply risk
item.description: Oil prices climbed more than 1% on Wednesday after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia renewed concerns around supply risks from the major exporter.
item.dc:creator: Colleen Howe, Jeslyn Lerh
item.content:encoded: Oil prices climbed more than 1% on Wednesday after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia renewed concerns around supply risks from the major exporter. Brent crude futures gained $1.59, or 1.4%, to $115.47 a barrel as of 0435 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude rose $1.43 or 1.4% to $101.33. Yemen's Iran-aligned [USN:L6N46D0XG TEXT:"Houthis"] said on Tuesday they had hit Saudi Arabia's biggest oil refinery with a missile, intensifying their strikes against the world's second-largest crude producer. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the strike on the 550,000 barrel-per-day facility. Prices swung higher after [USN:L2N46D00J TEXT:"dropping"] nearly $2 on Tuesday. For now, the market is still pricing in a greater likelihood of re-escalation, ING commodity strategists said on Wednesday. "Oil prices remain elevated as the market waits for greater clarity on President Trump's next move toward Iran," said ING strategists. "If we get past the elections without renewed strikes on Iran, that might be enough for the market's risk premium to start eroding," they added. Meanwhile, US crude oil stocks eased, according to market sources citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Crude stocks fell by 2.03 million barrels in the week ended October 23, the sources said. However, analysts polled by Reuters estimated that crude inventories rose by about 15,000 barrels in the week. The market awaits the US Energy Information Administration's official weekly inventory report, due later in the day, for more clarity. The market will also monitor an upcoming industry meeting on Sunday, where OPEC+ oil producers are expected to keep their December [USN:L6N46D0JQ TEXT:"oil output targets"] steady, according to people with knowledge of the matter. Production in most of the seven core OPEC+ members — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman — is below their output targets. Crude oil exports from Russia's Baltic and Black Sea ports could [USN:L6N46D0WL TEXT:"fall"] next month as domestic refiners increase diesel output following a deal with Washington this month, traders said.

item.title: Stocks get AI lift, kiwi slides on RBNZ's surprise hold
item.description: Asia stocks rallied on Wednesday as renewed AI enthusiasm buoyed sentiment ahead of earnings from industry bellwethers later in the US day, while the New Zealand dollar tumbled after the country's central bank unexpectedly held rates steady.
item.dc:creator: Rae Wee
item.content:encoded: Asia stocks rallied on Wednesday as renewed AI enthusiasm buoyed sentiment ahead of earnings from industry bellwethers later in the US day, while the New Zealand dollar tumbled after the country's central bank unexpectedly held rates steady. South Korea's Kospi (.KS11) surged more than 6% and was on track for its largest one-day percentage gain since July 31, after chipmaker SK Hynix (000660.KS) reported a more than seven-fold jump in quarterly profit and said it would [USN:L2N46D1DE TEXT:"return about $75 billion"] to shareholders this year. The AI rally faces its next test when [USN:L3N46D1FP TEXT:"technology giants"] Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Microsoft (MSFT.O) report earnings after market close, with investors looking for evidence of returns that would justify the hefty cost of the AI build-out. "The equity market has been pricing it as a growth opportunity. The credit markets have started to price the financing risk," said Nick Ferres, chief investment officer of Vantage Point Asset Management. "While the capex boom continues - and it does look like the major companies are going to confirm or affirm the capex... the demand side still looks reasonably strong, but there's a question mark over the return on investment. On the financing side, the financing markets have become more challenged for maybe the weaker balance sheet players." In Asia, MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) was up 1.7%, with Japan's Nikkei (.N225) adding 1.1% and China's CSI300 blue-chip index (.CSI300) advancing 0.7%. Nasdaq futures added 0.35% and S&P 500 futures edged up 0.05%. EUROSTOXX 50 futures and DAX futures were down more than 0.2%. A series of AI-related [USN:L3N46C0RT TEXT:"funding announcements"] from Meta (META.O) , SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Broadcom (AVGO.O) this week has breathed new life into the AI trade, with [USN:L6N46C148 TEXT:"Anthropic's"] filing for an initial public offering also providing support. "Not all big tech stocks should be treated equally regarding future potential growth. The period of a rising market lifting all stocks has started to shift," said Chris Brigati, SWBC's chief investment officer. "Future expectations are more focused upon execution risk and how much future success is already embedded in the current stock price." CENTRAL BANK SURPRISES Earnings aside, investors are watching for the [USN:L6N46915P TEXT:"Bank of Canada"] and [USN:L6N46518P TEXT:"the Fed's"] respective policy decisions later on Wednesday. , <0#USDIRPR> Expectations are for the BoC to raise rates and the Fed to keep them on hold, though analysts at JPMorgan said in a client note that they anticipated at least two hawkish dissents for the US central bank. "Market participants will likely focus on how Chair (Kevin) Warsh couches the decision, and we think deferring on an explanation will be viewed as dovish in nature," they said. Earlier on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand [USN:L6N46E02E TEXT:"surprised the markets"] by holding its benchmark official cash rate at 2.75% in a narrow vote, sending the kiwi down more than 1% to a session-low of $0.5583. "Markets were too confident about a hike today, but that does not necessarily mean the entire rate outlook is overpriced," said Carol Kong, a currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia. "Today's decision shows the RBNZ is willing to surprise markets, a reminder that central banks do not take orders from markets." In other currencies, the Australian dollar steadied at $0.7031, buoyed by data which showed [USN:L2N46E02G TEXT:"domestic inflation"] accelerated in the third quarter as fuel prices increased. Israel's shekel weakened after exit polls showed the country's [USN:L2N46D04I TEXT:"wartime election"] appeared deadlocked. Elsewhere, oil prices rose after an [USN:L3N46E029 TEXT:"attack on a refinery"] in Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest crude exporter, renewed concerns around the risks to supply in the Middle East. Brent crude futures were up 1.4% to $115.47 a barrel, while US crude rose 1.5% to $101.40 per barrel. Spot gold fell 0.4% to $4,040.32 an ounce.

item.title: Vietnam considering cutting gasoline tax, electricity prices
item.description: Vietnam is considering cutting its special consumption tax on all gasoline grades to zero from next month and may reduce retail electricity prices to help households and businesses, the government said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vietnam is considering cutting its special consumption tax on all gasoline grades to zero from next month and may reduce retail electricity prices to help households and businesses, the government said. Vietnam is facing upward pressure on inflation and risks missing this year's economic growth target of at least 10% The proposed special consumption tax cut would apply from November 1 through to March 31 next year, the government said late on Tuesday Vietnam is targeting inflation at 4.5% this year. Annual inflation was 5.08%, in September and 4.89% in August, according to official data Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Van Thang on Tuesday told the finance ministry to review the legal basis, feasibility and impact of reducing the special consumption tax on gasoline to zero, the government said The tax on gasoline currently ranges from 7% to 10% Thang told state utility EVN to recalculate its costs and maximise savings to allow for a a cut in the average retail electricity tariff Vietnam's economy [USN:P8N3YL023 TEXT:"grew 9.95%"] in the third quarter and fourth quarter growth must be higher than 12% to meet the 10% annual target

item.title: OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips, The Information reports
item.description: OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips, The Information reported on Tuesday, citing a person familiar with the matter, as technology companies ramp up spending to meet surging demand for AI computing.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: OpenAI plans to buy Google's (GOOGL.O) AI chips, The Information reported on Tuesday, citing a person familiar with the matter, as technology companies [USN:L3N46A020 TEXT:"ramp up"] spending to meet surging demand for AI computing. The reported plan would deepen ties between OpenAI and Alphabet's Google, which compete in AI products and search but have increasingly struck commercial deals. Last week, OpenAI said it would make its [USN:L6N4661GK TEXT:"frontier AI models"] available through Google Cloud. The report did not disclose financial terms or other details. Google did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours, while OpenAI declined to comment. Amazon (AMZN.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Google parent Alphabet plan to spend as much as $600 billion combined this year on AI infrastructure as investors increasingly question when such spending will translate into meaningful returns. OpenAI is already among the largest buyers of Nvidia's (NVDA.O) graphics processing units (GPUs), which it uses to train and deploy AI models. Reuters reported in June 2025 that the ChatGPT maker [USN:L4N3SU17K TEXT:"had begun renting"] Google's AI chips. Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) have gained traction as [USN:L4N41C2LT TEXT:"an alternative"] to Nvidia's market-leading AI chips as companies seek cheaper options. Google began selling TPUs directly to some customers this year. Alphabet will report its quarterly results later on Wednesday, with investors looking for signs that its heavy investment in AI is continuing to drive growth in its cloud business. Deals with customers including rival Anthropic have fueled demand for Google's TPUs. Alphabet expects to begin recognizing a small percentage of revenue from TPU sales agreements by the end of this year, with the vast majority expected to be recognized in 2027, CFO Anat Ashkenazi previously said. OpenAI in June unveiled its [USN:L6N42V15J TEXT:"first custom AI chip"] designed with Broadcom (AVGO.O) , and said it planned to deploy the processor by the end of this year as part of a multi-generation chip program.

item.title: Cooper Flagg leads Mavericks into clash with ailing, unbeaten Thunder
item.description: Coming off one of the best games of his young career, Cooper Flagg and the Dallas Mavericks face a different type of challenge when they host the Oklahoma City Thunder on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Coming off one of the best games of his young career, Cooper Flagg and the Dallas Mavericks face a different type of challenge when they host the Oklahoma City Thunder on Wednesday. In Dallas' four-point victory over Miami on Monday, Flagg tied his career high with 11 assists and set a career best with five steals to go along with 29 points. "That's one thing about Coop, the ball comes out of his hands at the right time," Mavericks coach Dusty May said. "If we get to where we're really finding a rhythm offensively, he's going to have some 15-20 assist games. There's no question." Flagg might not need to reach those lofty numbers against a short-handed Thunder team, but Dallas figures to need a strong performance from its young star against one of the league's top defensive teams. Oklahoma City swept all three games against Dallas last season. Flagg averaged just 9.0 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists in the two games he played against the Thunder. All three figures were his lowest against any opponent during his rookie season. The Thunder are coming off an emotional 125-114 home victory over Phoenix on Monday in their first game without starters Jalen Williams (fractured left fibula and dislocated ankle) and Cason Wallace (left shoulder). Both players sustained their injuries in Sunday's victory over the Clippers, with each facing an extended absence. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander always sets the tone for Oklahoma City, but his leadership is under even greater scrutiny as the Thunder navigate the early stages of life without the injured starters. "He's amazing in every situation," Oklahoma City coach Mark Daigneault said. "But he's amazing in this situation. His ability to empathize with his teammates and lead in the next competitive battle." Ajay Mitchell's role expanded last season when Williams missed extended time, and the guard will be called upon again in his teammate's absence. Mitchell scored a career-high 30 points in Monday's victory. "Zoom out to his whole trajectory as a player, he was pretty functional and impactful even as a rookie player on a very good team," Daigneault said of Mitchell. "... He's kind of established that he's a great player and that he's got a really bright future." The Thunder will also be looking for greater contributions from rookies Aday Mara, Bennet Stirtz and Josh Dix. "We don't really have a choice," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "Those guys are going to be thrown into the fire. Ultimately they'll get better from those experiences. We'll get better from those experiences." With Williams and Wallace potentially sidelined for the remainder of the season, Oklahoma City will need to find more ways to win despite having a less experienced roster than the one that finished with the NBA's best record last season. "We're a no-excuse team," Isaiah Hartenstein said. "Guys have to step up, and we trust everybody on the court." Center Chet Holmgren (right knee) will miss his second consecutive game for Oklahoma City, while guard Alex Caruso will also sit out after spraining his right ankle in Monday's win. The Thunder are just the second team in NBA history to open three consecutive seasons with four straight wins. A victory Wednesday would make them the first team ever to win their first five games in three consecutive seasons. Wednesday's game begins a stretch in which Dallas will play six of seven games at home. For Oklahoma City, it marks the start of a stretch in which the Thunder will play eight of 10 games on the road. Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving (left knee) is listed as questionable. Rookie guard Sergio De Larrea will miss the game after spraining his right knee in Monday's victory. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bringing the Middle Ages to modern China, medieval combat finds a foothold
item.description: Around 80 fighters in steel armour stormed across a Beijing park on an otherwise quiet Saturday, their swords, axes and polearms clanging against shields in a spectacle that echoed a medieval battlefield.
item.dc:creator: Shubing Wang, Huey Leong
item.content:encoded: Around 80 fighters in steel armour stormed across a Beijing park on an otherwise quiet Saturday, their swords, axes and polearms clanging against shields in a spectacle that echoed a medieval battlefield. Among them was Guan Xiaoqi, nicknamed "Postman", who traded his desk job for 30 kilograms (66 lb) of steel armour and a passion for participating in full-contact medieval combat tournaments. Now a martial arts coach, Guan is helping to grow China's medieval combat community, hoping to turn the niche pastime into a widely recognised sport. "It's a sport that can bring excitement and passion to young people," he said, adding that participation had risen steadily in recent years. Guan said the physically demanding combat tests not only strength but mental endurance, with competitors battling in heavy armour until their opponents are brought down. "We're all equally exhausted. If you think you're the most tired, you're probably just making excuses for yourself. If others can persevere, so can I," said participant Zhang Chao, describing the sense of achievement that comes with every contest. Known internationally as "buhurt", the modern sport emerged from medieval re-enactment communities in Eastern Europe and has grown into a global competition circuit. It arrived in China about a decade ago and has since attracted a small but growing following in cities such as Beijing and Shanghai. With overseas teams joining the competition, Guan said the event in Beijing, Shanhe Cup Full-Contact Armored Combat Open, offered Chinese athletes a rare opportunity to measure themselves against more experienced opponents from countries including Italy, Russia and France. While acknowledging the Chinese athletes' shortcomings, he remained optimistic about the country's progress. "Now that we've seen where we fall short, we know what we need to work on to close the gap," he said.

item.title: Three South Korean financial firms including Bithumb report data breaches, Yonhap says
item.description: Three South Korean financial firms reported data breaches on Wednesday, the Yonhap News Agency said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Three South Korean financial firms reported data breaches on Wednesday, the Yonhap News Agency said. Here are some details: Crypto exchange Bithumb said its in-house mobile system had been hacked and personal information leaked, Yonhap reported. It was investigating whether member data was included. Brokerage Daishin Securities said about 38,000 pieces of customer information had been leaked and that it had taken emergency measures, according to Yonhap. Asset manager Mirae Asset Global Investments had also confirmed a hacking incident, and authorities were assessing the situation, the report said. Spokespeople for Bithumb, Daishin and Mirae Asset could not be immediately reached for comment. The incidents follow a wave of hacking attacks at 16 South Korean financial firms, including banks, causing around 100,000 cases of data leaks so far, according to the Financial Services Commission (FSC) earlier this month. Separately, Seoul's Science Ministry and the Korea Internet & Security Agency have urged website operators to check for PHP flaws. The flaws let attackers run malicious commands on a server without logging in.

item.title: US costs of Iran war rise to over $47 billion, according to Pentagon estimate
item.description: The US military has spent over $47 billion so far to prosecute the war in Iran, more than 25% higher than the Defense Department's estimate in July, according to Pentagon data obtained by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Phil Stewart
item.content:encoded: The US military has spent over $47 billion so far to prosecute the war in Iran , more than 25% higher than the Defense Department's estimate in July, according to Pentagon data obtained by Reuters. The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment on its estimate, which has not been shared publicly. The disclosure about the rising cost of the Iran war comes as Republicans wrestle with the political fallout of the unpopular conflict ahead of the November 3 election that will determine control of Congress for the next two years. The war's impact on global energy costs has weighed on support for Republican candidates and hurt President Donald Trump's approval ratings. Trump's Republican Party holds a narrow majority in both chambers of Congress. The Pentagon's latest estimate was tied to the operational costs of carrying out the war, with a projected cost of more than $29 billion to replace expended munitions used in the conflict. More than $6 billion would be needed to replace military equipment and so-called "platform losses," which include the loss of aircraft including many drones lost during the war. Trump launched the Iran war jointly with Israel in February, predicting that the conflict would last a short time. Trump's initial strategy in the Iran war focused on first using expensive, high-end precision missiles to bomb Iran's defenses so it could later use less expensive munitions, including gravity bombs like the air-launched JDAMs, which are plentiful. But [USN:L6N40R14K TEXT:"an April ceasefire"] gave time for Iran to dig out underground storage facilities, bringing back online some Iranian defenses, as well as missiles and drones that had been inaccessible. Trump has since imposed a naval blockade on Iran to starve it of oil export revenue and held out the possibility of [USN:S0N45A05U TEXT:"restarting combat operations after the midterm elections"]. US officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, say the Pentagon has been planning to restart heavy fighting if ordered to do so. The latest Pentagon estimate compares to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's July estimate of $37.5 billion for the cost of the war. While the figures include a host of operational costs, from flight operations to cyber support, the US military's Iran war cost estimates did not clearly account for the massive expense expected to repair damage to US bases sustained by Iranian missile and drone attacks.

item.title: Polarized zinc becomes a bull-bear battleground
item.description: Record long and short positions have locked zinc bulls and bears in a standoff on the London Metal Exchange (LME).
item.dc:creator: Andy Home
item.content:encoded: Record long and short positions have locked zinc bulls and bears in a standoff on the London Metal Exchange (LME). The fund community is split down the middle over whether this year's [USN:L8N3YS0VM TEXT:"unexpected price rally"] is over or merely pausing for breath. Investment managers have accumulated record short positions on the London zinc contract. But fund long positioning is also close to record highs. The tension is manifest in outright price volatility and a rolling squeeze on nearby dates. The conspicuous absence of any price consensus reflects an equally polarized physical market, neatly captured by the International Lead and Zinc Study Group (ILZSG) in its latest statistical snapshot. EXPECTED FEAST TURNS TO FAMINE When ILZSG met this time last year, it expected robust mine supply and higher refined production to overwhelm demand to the tune of a 271,000-metric-ton surplus. The group's latest assessment is that the global market will experience an 88,000-ton supply shortfall this year. The revision is all down to what's been happening on the supply side. Demand is barely growing, reflecting zinc's exposure via galvanized steel to the construction sector, which is weak everywhere, particularly in China. But zinc supply has surprised on the downside. Rather than growing as expected, global mined zinc output is on track to fall by 2.6% year-on-year in 2026, reflecting a combination of the closure of Glencore's (GLEN.L) [USN:L4N3BN4VH TEXT:"Lady Loretta mine"] in Australia, lower grades at Teck Resources' (TECKb.TO) Red Dog mine in Alaska and unexpected disruption at Boliden's (BOL.ST) [USN:L8N41B0BN TEXT:"Garpenberg"] mine in Sweden. Tight raw-materials markets have pushed smelter treatment charges into uncharted negative territory, leaving many smelters living off sales of by-products such as sulphuric acid. Chinese smelters are winning the intense competition for zinc concentrates. China's refined output is expected to rise by 3.7% this year from 2025, but production in the rest of the world is due to contract by 2.0%. The result is a polarized physical market, with China in surplus and everyone else short of metal. CHINA'S EXPORT SURGE [USN:L8N44L13M TEXT:"Chinese exports"] are helping rebalance the global market, thanks to a widening arbitrage window with the LME. China shipped 111,000 tons of refined zinc in August and September, according to the World Bureau of Metal Statistics, which collects official customs figures. Flows have unsurprisingly been directed to LME warehouse locations such as Hong Kong, Singapore and the Taiwanese port of Kaohsiung. China has traditionally been a net importer of refined zinc, and the last time it exported such volumes was 20 years ago, before Beijing imposed export tariffs in 2008. ROLLING SQUEEZE China's deliveries have helped LME stocks recover from an August low of 92,550 tons to 165,650 tons, but the arrivals are being quickly snapped up. Last week brought 26,300 tons of net cancellations, and the amount of metal now awaiting physical load-out has grown to almost 20% of the headline stocks total. Off-warrant inventory, meanwhile, remains extremely low at just 11,261 tons. The rolling squeeze that has gripped the LME contract since July is becoming more acute again. The cash premium over three-month metal has flared out from under $50 per ton to $118 per ton over the last week. Three-month zinc has bounced off the October 15 low of $3,650 per ton to a Tuesday high of $3,855, which suggests the bulls have the upper hand. For how long remains to be seen. RELIEF NEXT YEAR? Zinc bears can take heart from ILZSG's forecasts for next year. The group expects mined supply to grow by 3.0% year-on-year in 2027, flipping the global market back to a modest 25,000-ton supply surplus. That, however, is a very marginal call in what is a 14-million-ton global marketplace. It also comes with the caveat that ILZSG was expecting mine production to grow this year, which is not how things have turned out. Short-term dynamics will be determined by whether China can maintain this pace of exports. Even China's super-competitive smelters seem to be struggling to access raw material. The country's imports of zinc concentrates grew by 30% year-on-year in 2025 but inbound volumes were up by just 0.6% year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026. Right now, there is still everything to fight for and the bull-bear battle looks set to continue for a while yet. (The opinions expressed here are those of Andy Home , a columnist for Reuters.)
